title: Bellissima, ma un po’ di cose da migliorare.
body:
L’app è stupenda e molto originale, la migliore per questo scopo sullo store a mio parere.
Ma ci sono un po’ di cose che secondo me vanno fatte notare e migliorate:
- ad esempio, non è possibile che ogni volta che mi suona una sveglia che se non sento e spengo entro 6 secondi mi fa morire gli alberi (con Apple). Sistemate sta cosa per favore!!! (perché ci sono 6 secondi “bonus” per uscire dall’app e ritornarci senza far morire l’albero)
- sarebbe bello se si aggiungessero più trofei e più missioni per ottenere monete e soprattutto gemme gratuitamente, che sono solo a pagamento e servono per sbloccare alberi speciali
- sarebbe bello anche aumentare le specie di alberi nel negozio
- infine, un’opzione che secondo me farebbe salire l’app ad un livello superiore rispetto ad ogni altra sarebbe quella di mettere un collegamento con Spotify per impostare e scegliere la musica che si ascolta durante lo studio o qualsiasi altra attività uno faccia con Forest, senza che venga contato come fuoriuscita dall’app
Spero che possiate attuare questi suggerimenti al più presto che per rendere l’app degna di avere 5 stelle e anche più!
Grazie🌈

Ad ogni modo, voglio riportare che la funzionalità “ritarda l’inizio di giornata” non sembra funzionare.

title: Migliorabile
body:
In generale reputo questa app molto valida, ancora devo scoprire tutto il nuovo aggiunto ma per ora sembra che sia stato migliorato ciò che doveva essere migliorato per un analisi accurata.
Dunque in quanto a funzionalità, questa app è perfetta.
Manca però un po’ di libertà estetica, cioè tanto per cominciare io vorrei avere la possibilità di modificare le etichette (nome e colore) dopo averle fatte, e magari eliminarle, se fossero state create per sbaglio.
Poi vorrei avere la possibilità di spostare gli alberi del mio giardino, insomma l’app funziona, ma per renderla perfetta credo che queste piccolezze siano d’obbligo.
Grazie per il lavoro che fate.

title: App stra consigliata
body: Anche se su ios è a pagamento, devo dire che ne vale la pena pagare per quest’app. È molto bella e mi piace un sacco questa cosa che, con un tot di monete, anche se io non ci sono ancora arrivata, si possa comprare un albero vero per ridurre il problema della deforestazione, del surriscaldamento globale ecc.. davvero una bella iniziativa. Un’altra cosa che mi piace è che ci siano dei suoni che puoi ascoltare, mentre metti il timer, sulla natura e sugli animali. Sono molto rilassanti. Stra consigliata e davvero molto carina. L’unica pecca è che per piantare un vero albero ci vogliano davvero tante monete, considerando che ogni 15 min te ne da solo 4 e tu devi arrivare a 2500. per il resto è davvero una bella app che consiglio a tutti quelli che vogliono contribuire a salvare il pianeta.
author: serena"

title: Non funziona
body:
Ho comprato l’app ormai mesi fa, e dopo pochi giorni di utilizzo lo store, gli achievements, e la sincronizzazione hanno smesso di funzionare per un errore sconosciuto. Contatto gli amministratori il 20 ottobre, che rispondono una volta ogni 3 settimane (se ti va bene!) e ad oggi stanno ancora “lavorando al problema”. I miei ultimi messaggi, risalenti a un mese fa, chiedevano se fosse possibile sincronizzare l’account manualmente visto che devo formattare il telefono e perderei tutte le monetine. Ancora nessuna risposta. 
Non che sia indispensabile acquistare nuovi alberi dallo store o sbloccare gli achievements eh, ma se pago un’app come minimo deve funzionare sia lei che la sua assistenza.

title: Bellissima applicazione, ma con le sue pecche
body:
Applicazione interessante, utile per chi, come me, ha problemi a gestire al meglio il suo tempo e a limitare l’uso dello smartphone. Tuttavia, la versione per iOs potrebbe migliorare:
1) Innanzitutto, non è possibile creare la “lista bianca” con le applicazioni utilizzabili anche in modalità concentrazione intensiva. Ciò risulta alquanto limitante nel momento in cui è necessario, ad esempio, fare una ricerca su google o leggere un messaggio importante
2) Le notifiche per piantare in gruppo non sempre arrivano, anzi: sono più le volte in cui gli inviti non vengono visualizzati correttamente rispetto a quelle in cui ciò avviene.

Queste sono le due ragioni per cui non riesco a dare cinque stelle a questa quasi-impeccabile applicazione. Gradirei dunque che risolveste al più presto quantomeno il problema degli inviti, al fine di potervi scrivere una recensione ancor più positiva.

title: Utilissima, ma con qualche difetto fastidioso
body: Ho provato diverse app il cui intento era quello di aiutare a concentrarsi, ma Forest è decisamente la migliore. È strutturata in modo simpatico, ti permette di studiare “con” i tuoi amici e ti stimola a voler completare la tua foresta, quasi fosse un gioco. Inoltre mi piace molto la possibilità di poter aiutare a piantare un albero vero, in questo modo studiando ti rendi anche utile all’ambiente. Non le do 5 stelle perché trovo che su IOS sia ottimizzata un po’ male, poiché non è possibile inserire l’opzione “non far appassire il tuo albero quando esci dall’app” quando utilizzi la modalità studio intensivo, l’unico modo per non far appassire l’albero è disattivare la modalità studio intensivo, ma in questo modo si ha la possibilità di usare altre applicazioni che ovviamente va a inficiare sulla concentrazione. Ritengo sia un problema soprattutto perché mi è capitato più di una volta di sbloccare il telefono (non ero uscita dall’app avevo solo bloccato il telefono, opzione consentita) dopo che il tempo settato era finito e di trovare l’albero morto.... eppure durante l’ora che avevo impostato non ho preso nemmeno una volta il cellulare, mi sono solo arrivate delle notifiche. Sinceramente è un po’ frustrante quindi spero possa essere risolto. A parte questo problema, l’app è magnifica e, tra tutte quelle che ho provato, è l’unica che veramente mi ha aiutato a concentrarmi nello studio.

title: Carina!
body: È un’app divertente per passare il tempo e rimanere più concentrati. Per me funziona: facendo sessioni di studio non troppo lunghe alla volta, metto in atto un meccanismo per cui “devo arrivare alla fine, mancano solo x minuti” e senza accorgermene riesco a studiare molto di più per volta, non distraendomi così frequentemente. Divertente.

title: more apps like this!
body:
i'm very excited about this app which i've been using for a few months now after hearing of it on a podcast.

things i think are amazing:
💚 interface. okay, i love a clean, simple, minimal design. also how their notifications and messages are phrased. very subtle, never passive aggressive.
💚 you can track what you are focusing on and change the categories. 
💚 you can get extra coins if you focus longer than you set a timer for.
💚 it's just well made, thought through, simple & easy.
💚 it has a calming rainforest music effect if you want white noise!! in app!!
💚 it does allow you to leave the app for a SPLIT second if you have an emergency or exit by accident, and the notification about a dying tree is still phrased very gently.
💚 there's initiatives like tests or wallpaper makers.
💚 idk why, but even if it's virtual (for now) the thought of the tree actually keeps me off my phone. even on things that could be urgent or where it would just be polite to answer right away. 
💚 i can't wait to be able to plant a real tree!!

things i'd love if this app had them:
🌻if the whitelist app function worked (i sometimes need reference pictures and i can't "flash that" like a music skip or something)
🌻 switch off notifications from within the app, because otherwise i forget to switch them back on for years
🌻 allow you to pick contacts who are excepted and whose calls you can take
🌻 classical music options
🌻 if there was some way to create a community with strangers, since irl friends won't likely use the invitation

it may seem like a bummer that this app isn't free, but other than ALL the points i made above: 
⭐️ it has no ads! besides from developers (discreet) there are never pop up ads or other sorts of flashy and annoying stuff
⭐️ actual tree planting needs funding. if it was only for the digital forest, i wouldn't have invested 3€. but real trees and the people who plant them deserve and need the financial support.

title: La miglior applicazione
body: Potrebbe essere considerato paradossale il fatto che l’utilizzo di un’applicazione richieda che tu non utilizzi il cellulare, non è mai esistita, o meglio, ci sono già state app di questo tipo, ma credo che questa sia quella più perfezionata. Design fantastico: un’app molto green. A livello ambientale può essere messa ai pari di Ecosia in quanto sia una delle poche che ti consente di piantare un albero di tua iniziativa, per farlo basta non usare il cellulare, e questo credo unisca la produttività personale (studio, sport e vita sociale) e ambientalismo. È bellissimo pensare come puoi fare il tuo piccolo per questo mondo distrutto (principalmente con la deforestazione appunto) con un’app. Spero che ci saranno in futuro applicazioni green come questa. Non ho mai comprato un’applicazione, questa è la prima volta che ho ritenuto sensato spendere dei soldi per un’applicazione.

title: App stupenda
body:
Sebbene possa, a primo impatto, sembrare un sistema banale e futile, ritengo che quest’applicazione abbia il prezzo che MERITA di avere. 
Sviluppa - nel tempo, non solo quando la si utilizza - la tua capacità di rimanere concentrato, ma rispecchia anche le esigenze di chi vuole “staccare la spina” dal proprio smartphone, dimenticarlo per un attimo e guardarsi intorno. 
Inoltre il supporto alla causa ambientalista è una chicca che, soprattutto al giorno d’oggi, può essere alquanto apprezzabile.

title: Un metodo più che efficace!
body:
Sono una ragazza che tende molto a perdere la concentrazione tra cellulare e altro quando si parla di studio, ma con questa app, tolgo tutte le distrazioni!
È veramente geniale l’applicazione in se, perchè se vuoi collezionare più alberi, li puoi comprare con le monete che riceverai solo con il tempo in cui starai staccato dal cellulare, e quindi non puoi non uscire dall’applicazione, perchè non solo non riceverai le monete, ma l’albero morirà.
Lo trovo molto geniale ed efficace, complimenti davvero alla mente di tutto ciò!

title: Mindfulness e "gamificazione" per la produttività
body:
È possibile impostare dai 10 minuti alle due ore, e il senso è come la tecnica "Pomodoro" dei 25 minuti+5 di riposo, solo che il tempo si può variare in base al proprio stato e al proprio obiettivo. La sfida è sempre quella di non toccare il telefono per il tempo a cui ci si compromette: se arriva una chiamata l'albero muore lo stesso di default, ma è possibile impostarlo in modo che almeno si prendano la metà dei punti. Io personalmente uso sempre la modalità "non disturbare" con tutte le mie eccezioni dei contatti già impostate.
Carina la divisione in cespugli (fino a 20 minuti), e alberi con vari livelli (dai 25 min). 
Il sistema di monete consente di comprare nuovi alberi e "white noise" di sottofondo. 
Se si imposta il "non disturbare" il white noise peraltro è l'unico modo per rendersi conto se il tempo è finito/è cresciuto l'albero (si interrompe qualunque rumore), perché la notifica di Forest viene anch'essa silenziata.
Ma in genere è meglio, anche perché superare il limite impostato consente di "potenziare" l'albero (ma va cambiato apposta, non è di default). 
Naturalmente bisogna essere onesti con se stessi e obbligarsi davvero a fare qualcosa di produttivo (dal lavoro alle faccende di casa), e nn limitarsi solo a non sbloccare il telefono e usare qualsiasi altra app (che implacabilmente stoppa tutto e uccide l'albero).
La competizione con altre persone nel mondo nn serve, a mio parere: ognuno lo imposta a modo suo (per esempio io il lavoro nn lo considero perché uso il telefono per diverse cose) e nn si è confrontabili.

Nel complesso, una unica app per obbligarti a fare una e una sola cosa alla volta, sfidarti a fare il tuo giardino quotidiano/settimanale/mensile più o meno deserto e sbloccare nuovi premi, oppure comprare un albero VERO nel mondo. Fa anche da white noise per concentrarsi meglio.
Infine "taggando" i propri alberi e cespugli fa anche da app di tracking del proprio tempo, utilizzando le statistiche integrate.

A me ha cambiato davvero tanto, app comsigliatissima.

title: Lo adoro.
body:
Questa applicazione mi ha veramente cambiato l’approccio allo studio. Il fatto di non poter utilizzare il telefono e la crescita di un albero permette un’alta concentrazione su quello che si sta facendo. 
Inoltre è bellissima l’idea di poter accumulare, grazie alle ore di concentrazione, dei “soldi” per comprare le diverse specie di fiori e alberi; è uno stimolo in più per utilizzare l’app. 
Ho molto apprezzato anche le study room che permettono lo studio di gruppo con altre persone, anche non conosciute. 
Questa app la consiglio veramente a chi cerca un modo per eliminare le distrazioni.

title: Problemi recenti
body:
Mi piace tanto quest’app, è bella e stimolante.
Ma recentemente ha dei problemi sul mio telefono:
• Non mi avvisa più quando il tempo è finito e l’albero è stato piantato. Cosa importantissima per me per organizzare le sessioni di studio.
• Lascio la app aperta con il telefono bloccato ma se apro il telefono per qualche motivo non c’è l’app e devo ricliccarci su per vedere l’albero che cresce. In più, talvolta ho iniziato a far crescere un albero e controllando più in là il tempo rimasto ho visto che l’app si era chiusa e l’albero non c’era più!

Per favore, mettete un nuovo aggiornamento e aggiustate questi problemi gravi. Non mi va di aver pagato per un’app che poi inizia a presentare questi problemi, io facevo tanto affidamento su questo metodo.

title: Ben fatta, ma si puó migliorare! Leggete!
body:
Mi piace come applicazione, è ben fatta e abbastanza semplice da usare. 
L’unico difetto che ho trovato è che essa stessa rischia di essere un limite per lo studio, quando questo richiede l’uso del telefono. Ad esempio la calcolatrice o un’app specifica (ad esempio io utilizzo un’applicazione di matematica quando faccio esercizi per riuscire a capire meglio i passaggi difficili che immediatamente non capisco) o anche il cronometro ad esempio, che a me spesso serve per tenere i tempi degli esercizi che eseguo, o banalmente, anche youtube è una buona risorsa per lo studio. 
Il computer non è sempre comodo e immediato per fare tutte queste cose.
Consiglierei di introdurre nelle impostazioni dell’app Forest una sorta di “on/off” di tutte le applicazioni presenti sul cellulare, tutte pre impostate sull’off, in modo che si possano mettere in “on” solo quelle che ci interessa usare in quel momento (per lo studio, per lo sport o qualunque altra mansione). Così tutte le app impostate in off non potranno essere usate, altrimenti l’albero morirà, mentre quelle in on, potranno essere usate senza problemi.
Penso che questa potrebbe essere una buona idea, anche perchè chi usa forest penso che voglia tenere conto dei propri tempi e dei propri progressi, quindi non avrebbe senso imbrogliare mettendo in “on” i social network. Ma ne caso la pensiate diversamente, potreste sempre eliminare dalla scelta di impostazione “on/off” tutti i social, impedendone la modifica e mantenendoli costantemente in off. 
Spero di vedere quest’app migliorata in questo senso... Buona giornata!

title: Molto carina 🍀
body:
Ho bisogno di studiare e di concentrarmi sui libri per molte ore, e spesso mi capita di distrarmi con il telefono, che sia per un messaggio o per noia. Grazie a questa app ho ridotto drasticamente il tempo perso al telefono durante lo studio! La crescita dell'albero mi motiva a non usare il telefono perché altrimenti morirebbe, e sentirei di aver perso quei minuti di studio, visto che a fine giornata l'app fornisce il tempo totale che abbiamo occupato concentrandoci. Inoltre, sono sicura che tutti i minuti che mi conta l'app sono di effettivo e vero studio. 
L'app mi è stata consigliata dal blogger Thomas Frank. 
Do 4 stelle e non 5 perché secondo me 1,99 euro per questa app sono un po' tanti. È carina ed efficace, ma vale 1 euro, poiché lo stesso risultato si potrebbe ottenere con un timer e mettendo il telefono in modalità aerea. Questa app semplicemente rende il processo più carino e motivazionale.

Me parece una injusticia que me quieran obligar a pagar una nueva versión para obtener beneficios que ya tenía hasta el 2025. Era una MUY BUENA aplicación que se subió al tren de monetizar cada movimiento del usuario. AHORA ES UNA ESTAFA TREMENDA!!!! title: 버그 있어요
body:
질 사용하고 있습니다.
최근 업데이트 이후 버그가 있어 리뷰를 남깁니다.
즐겨찾기로 등록한 식물의 시간을 수정한 후 실행하면, 시간을 수정했다는 것만으로도 해당 식물이 즐겨찾기에 자동으로 등록됩니다.
이전에는 제가 직접 하트를 눌러야 즐겨찾기로 등록되었는데, 지금은 원치 않게 계속 추가되고 있습니다.
이 버그를 수정해 주세요.

Lo estoy usando bien.
Después de la última actualización, encontré un error y quiero dejar una reseña.
Si modifico el tiempo de una planta que ya está en favoritos y la ejecuto, automáticamente se vuelve a registrar en favoritos solo por haber cambiado el tiempo.
Antes, solo se añadían las plantas a las que yo les daba “me gusta”, pero ahora se agregan sin querer todo el tiempo.
Por favor, arreglen este error.

title: La app está bien, pero...
body:
Más de una vez he estado tan concentrado que no escucho cuando el tiempo termina. Aun con el volumen al máximo, el timbre es muy discreto y no hay manera de cambiarlo. Tampoco hay manera de que sea un timbre constante, como una alarma.

Por lo demás, el app me gusta, pero le doy una estrella porque el sonido es una funcionalidad que considero primordial y, a menos que permitan timbres constantes tipo alarma y la posibilidad de cambiar el tipo de timbre, no me sirve.

title: Mal diseñada, investiguen bien qué ofrece esta app en comparación con otras
body: Supongo que si uno va iniciándose con la técnica pomodoro esta app podría funcionar. El atractivo del porqué la compré fue el concepto de “ver” de manera fresca mis avances. Sin embargo tras comprarla quedé decepcionado por sus carencias y mala planeación para hacer la app. En comparación con otras apps que usan la técnica pomodoro, esta no permite salirte de app sin que muera tu árbol (la principal razón por la que compre la app), lo que no consideraron los creadores es que si utilizas tu ipad para la app y estás estudiando, necesitarás salirte para poder abrir las aplicaciones con las que estudiarás. Por esto, esta app me es inútil. Espero mi experiencia le pueda servir a algún otro posible comprador para que no malgaste su dinero.

Entonces tengo unas pocas monedas en mi iPad y me gustaría transferirlas a mi celular que es donde principalmente uso Forest y donde la cantidad de monedas que tengo es mayor.
Si nos dejaran transferir monedas de un usuario a otro sería genial. Muchas gracias!! P.d. Adoro Forest. Es un ejemplo de Retroalimentación positiva psicológica. ☺️👏🏼

I used to LOVE this app and not do without, and now every time I open it I end up frustrated. Wish I could have the old app back.

title: Great app
body:
I highly recommend this app to anyone.

I downloaded this app a few years ago, and it is well worth the money. In the end, it is only a few euros for a lifetime use, and it had a very significant effect on my social media consumption. 

I notice that my social media consumption steadily increases if I don’t use this app to control it, which is logical given how it stimulates screen time. After I use this app again for a while, I notice I pick-up my phone less even when I am free (and thus not actively restricting it).

title: Needs split screen and rotation
body:
I use an iPad Pro and to study. For a productivity app it’s weird that Forest does not support rotation and split screen.

- Split screen so you can have your timer open in a small window when you are reading a document or article.

- rotation so you can hold your iPad however you want. I usually have my iPad upside down when I lay in my bed, because when you have it upside down the charging port is on top. This way you don’t accidentally entangle yourself in the charging cable. However each time I tgo from another app back to Forest, I have to rotate my iPad 180 degrees, because Forest is one of the few apps that doesn’t support rotation.

You can set it up so you can still do other stuff on your device without consequences for your forest. Time  will even count down when you use a different app. Maybe this is a good thing as you will be able to grow your forest quicker and therefore buy your free trees asap. The earth needs it.

title: Great app, not so interesting content
body:
The idea behind the app is great and very effective. However the content of the forest is rather shallow. I understand that the developers tried to make it as simplistic as possible, so the user won’t be distracted, however I am a user who completely disables his distractions (social medias, youtube, etc) till 8:00 PM. While I take my pomodoro breaks I would like apply some creativity and make my forest appealing. In a way garnering it. Such content can be rivers, mountains etc. You can even add different biomes and the rivers or mountains can split those biomes, meaning you can use two or even three, why not. You got my point. 

Overall, great app for pomodoro, that shows your progress comprehensively enough.

title: Simple & effective
body:
Simple layout, simple system. Creates a quick & easy reward. Allows for short term attainable goals. I love being able to be like “okay, I need just 25 minutes of focus to get a reward, we can do this!” And generally it then brings me in a flow.
Additionally the new trees you unlock keep it fresh & exciting to set new challenges and get a new reward. 

Only downside: A lot of my friends already use the app, but it seems you can only connect new people & get rewards for that☹️.

title: Beautiful clean app
body:
Works great and I use it almost everyday. You can use it for study, work or other things you want. By labeling you can organize the things you do. It’s really addictive, because you don’t want the plants to die. But addictive in a good way. With coins that you earn you can buy different kinds of plants or trees. 

Also when you’re finished you can set a timer to take a break. So it’s really nice when you use the Pomodoro method. 

It’s a great app for people who have troubles with focusing, taking breaks or just want to improve there work/study time.

I don’t know if it’s aloud to do, but if you want to you can use my friend code: 5TTUKKSG
With this friendship award you earn 500 coins, so you can buy yourself a lovely tree to begin with. You just need to sign in and use this code. In the app you can go to store and then click on invite friends. Use the code and there you are.

So yes, I highly recommend this app.

title: Aan te raden voor studenten
body:
Forest voelt als een spelletje die het focussen op zichzelf een belonend gevoel geeft, niet slechts het eindresultaat wat wellicht niet motiverend genoeg is. Telkens groeit je bosje iets meer, en wanneer je je bosje gegroeid ziet voor de dag, voel je een vorm van bevrediging en trots. Zo wil je steeds beter worden in het focussen, omdat je later op de dag een direct resultaat ziet van de gefocuste minuten. Tevens brengt het meer structuur in de perioden dat je je voorneemt dat je zal focussen.
Zeker tijdens deze tijd van zelfstudie tijdens de Coronacrisis is deze geïnvesteerde twee euro lucratief geweest, veel lucratiever dan een koffie van twee euro waarvan je denkt dat dat de sleutel is om op je werk te kunnen gaan focussen. Deze mini-game is de sleutel.

Alleen geen 5 sterren omdat je blijkbaar maximaal maar 5 echte bomen kunt laten plaatsen met je gespaarde punten.

Ik schrijf deze review om een nieuw boompje te unlocken btw, maar ik liet me meeslepen omdat ik oprecht een grote waardering voel voor deze app.

Otherwise, Great app.

And it’s nice that you can choose how many minutes you want to focus or even stay focussed in groups. If one person of the group fails, all the persons trees of the group will die, so that’s an extra motivation. With coins you get for planting you can buy different kind of trees, just what you like.

title: Intuitive, to the point & helps with ADHD
body:
As a seasoned procrastinator with ADHD I’ve tried many things to make getting started (and staying on track) easier but nothing has been as simple in it’s effectiveness as this app. 
I can’t really put my finger on it what makes this app so nice; I suppose the fact that you staying focused creates something (an adorable digital tree and eventually potentially even an actual tree) makes working a bit more wholesome and enjoyable. 
Besides that, the consequence of the death of your precious tree (that you’ve already put 25 minutes in and would only take 15 more minutes to be fully grown) gives that extra nudge to, alright alright, keep working. 
As a distraction-sensitive ADHDer this app is a life saver for writing my thesis, I really recommend it.

PS: if you combine it with the desktop app on your computer it’s even better, for those who have to use a computer to work on with all those tempting websites a couple clicks away, that combo makes it fool proof for me.

body:

I don’t mind the option of having a Plus account, but it’s constantly shoved in your face to the point where it becomes annoying; I’m a student, and I used to find Forest the most relaxing way to track my sessions, but I’m liking the app less and less.

title: Once good, now only annoying
body: I bought this app back when it was a pay-once model. I loved it for years for its simplicity, that it does smth good in the world and cute designs. But now that picked it up again after a long break it is cluttered with subscription reminders showing you every step on the way what you miss out by not paying. They gave me a tree and terrain as compensation that I bought the app back in the day but tbh that is NOT what I want nor do I feel like this should be legal since they changed the terms of what I payed for. The app now feels too busy, less intuitive and there’s rumours that they use genAI. All in all I do not reccomend it anymore. It’s easier to light a tea light and work until it has extinguished. At least it won’t bombard me with useless stuff. And it’s cheaper too in bulk.
author: Rebecca Kilde

title: Frustrating downgrade
body: Forest has been my favorite productivity app for years, but the recent update feels like a downgrade. Adjusting the focus time has become unnecessarily complicated, when it used to be simple and intuitive. The new design also feels more childish and less polished than before, which takes away from the clean, focused experience I really liked about Forest. I hope you’ll reconsider these changes and bring back the simplicity and mature design that made the app so enjoyable to use - so I can spend less time adjusting my focus time and more time actually focusing.

title: Honestly the only app that has really worked for me
body: I have tried to find a way to stay focused for a long time. I’ve tried cleaning my space, moving place of study and downloaded a lot of apps. It always ends with me being behind schedule on everything because I am unable to cope with my methods. I was recommended to download “Forrest” from a company called Lanterna (deals with IB education and stuff). I stayed away from it in the beginning because it costed money, but realized after a while how little it was and downloaded it. The concept is genius. Combining a game with getting things done, playing on your conscience. I love it and would recommend it to anyone who struggles with staying focused and also everyone else. title: The best study tool for ADHDers!
body:
This app has been a godsend, and it’s the only app I’ve used for years consistently! I have ADHD, and studying (or just focusing in general) when my phone is around has always been such a struggle. With this app I’m able to challenge myself and leave my phone alone to grow my forest, and it gives me the dopamine boost I need when I see a new tree in my forest! 

I love the variety of trees you can plant! I’m currently saving up in-game coins to buy the doggo-tree, and I’m obsessed! 

I’ve recently started using it when being around friends and family as well, and I use it when I’m hanging out when my boyfriend to stay off my phone. It’s a great motivator to know that I’m able to stay in the moment more and be present, and get rewards for it!

If you’re like me and struggle to leave your phone alone I highly recommend this app! I’ve been recommending it to my friends, classmates, and ESPECIALLY my fellow ADHDers for years, and I can’t say it enough - this app is amazing!

I’d give it 15/10 stars if I could, but 5 will do for now. The only thing I would recommend while using the app is to turn off notifications, as it is insanely tempting to stop the stopwatch early.

For me, the interface would be better if it was simpler: easier to find friends on the app, no sections like tags or news or rooms or timeline, just focus on what you and your forest (and perhaps friends' too). title: My most helpful app
body:
I have a huge problem concentrating on anything at a given length of time. My mind keeps floating to other stuff, and I usually end up googling everything that comes to mind, checking to see if I’ve received any messages on my social medias, or just generally doing other things I should not do at that time on my phone.

With this app, I find I have an easier time working with what I’m supposed to. I usually set it to 25 minutes, and tell myself “now I’ll just work for 25 minutes, then have a break, and then see if I can’t work another 25 minutes afterwards”. And I can!
This was the best tool for me during exam preps and I simply cannot express how much value I’ve gotten out of it. And the fact that your points can be turned into a REAL tree?! Wow!
5/5 for a good reason!

This app "locks" your phone when you have planted a tree, and if you go to another app while you have a tree planted, it will die. No one wants a dead tree in their forest. It is nice to force you not to go on your phone while working/studying 😊 
When you have planted enough trees and have enough coins earned, you can either plant a real tree in Africa or you can choose to spend the coins on fancy trees you can plant on the app.

author: OdinOB

title: New visual appearance
body:
I loved this app for studying but the new visual appearance looks AI-generated (some of the developers other apps are AI based).  So disappointing considering that Forest is partially about planting *real life* trees, yet the technology used to produce these apps are actively killing them. So do you care about money or the environment?
Many people I know who used forest have stopped due to the new interface, it’s so off-putting.
author: fixyourstupidadvertisements

title: Successive updates ruined it
body: I’ve used Forest for 7 years, but it’s really gone downhill in the last year. The pushing for plus interrupts use of the app, the most recent update has made the design cartoonish, obnoxious, and in your face, the time guard feature pushing itself on me when I don’t expect it means that I regularly have to close the app and restart after accidentally clicking on it, time crystals and coins are useless as new trees are all through events instead of buying them, the app doesn’t notify me when my trees have grown about 80% of the time.  It’s become a source of stress rather than a useful and aesthetically pleasing focus tool.

title: ux design update just isn’t it..
body:
i have used this app religiously for years and it had been a great tracker for my productivity. i had mixed feelings ab the monthly sub news but glad i could keep my one-time sub alive. however, i most esp miss the favorites feature and how straightforward the ux used to be! 

this update makes me have to click so much more buttons to finish planting and i even have to wait through all the animations. i get the animations are pretty and all, but for a focus app, it’s a waste of time. i cant even view how much time in the day ive spent focusing anymore unless i check my actual forest. the favorites feature was also ironically my FAVORITE feature and it’s just gone, along with all of the favorites i had prepared in advance assigning trees per task. i really dont understand why this feature had to go???

besides all that, i do like the session title feature and how we have more options in the shop. visuals wise, i admit they also aren’t that bad. but honestly the things ive mentioned above really have been a bother to me as a regular user. 

my review is two stars and not one for my lingering love for the app, and im rating low in the hopes you can be able to notice. but i genuinely hope you can listen to your users seeing as there have been so many complaints everywhere and barely any movement. thank you.

title: It is buggy after the new UI overhaul
body:
The new UI overhaul has made the app significantly more frustrating to use. It feels like a major redesign was made without enough consideration for the existing user experience, and many things that used to be simple are now unintuitive and require additional steps.

On my end, the app is also extremely buggy. If I leave the app while a tree is growing, all of my apps become unlocked. Sometimes, when the timer finishes, the tree doesn't even get recorded. The app also randomly closes at times.

I really hope the team prioritizes stability and usability rather than continuing to add or change things unnecessarily. Forest was already a simple and effective productivity app, so the redesign feels like it has made the experience more complicated without adding much value. Please listen to the existing users and consider their feedback when making major UI changes.

body:
I like the new update, the new UI is clean and the addition of the “I’ll spend my time on…” makes it feel more intentional whenever you plant a tree. 

But I’m writing this review because I miss when the main page displayed your total focus time. AND ESPECIALLY the circle that we can use to adjust the focus time. You guys need to bring that back as it’s super handy and we can visualize the tree better and its different levels depending on the duration. The circle presenting the tree has increased in size in this update, I suggest reducing the circumference a bit to accommodate the circle dial.

Also, I miss when we could adjust the tag/label, the tree, and the duration all in one small tab. Now you have to open individual tabs for each one, so three interfaces have to be used to adjust each one which I think is inconvenient. And it covers up the entire screen, size can be reduced.

tldr: new update is aesthetic, but we lost features that made the service convenient.
author: Jaurse

Now there’s like two or more buttons I have to press to “collect rewards.” I also can’t see the time focused for the day in the planting part and have to actually go to the forest just to check, when back then it was already displayed. 

The new update definitely sacrificed a lot of the ease of use features for nothing. Hope you bring some of them back.

title: Account Lost after Update
body:
I bought the app years ago. Today, I was logged out of my account and was unable to re-login with Apple ID. I had years there—months worth of trees that helped me get back on track with school and work. Now, they’re just gone. I don’t get a refund either.

Edit: 1-2 years later. I didn’t get the gold or trees back, and it was disheartening at first, but that’s because I started to view them as proof or a metric of my productivity. I started to care more about the numbers than actually learning or working, rather than putting in the work. And from this loss, I learnt that this is just an app. You can work 8 hours, forget to log it, and feel bad that you won’t see it. But you know you worked, and you even did it without incentive. That’s worth a lot more. You can always start over because that drive was and has always been in you methinks.

9.75 / 10 app!

title: Forest is great but not on Apple Watch
body:
Forest has been really useful to me for focusing and getting things done. I just got an apple watch as a gift and wanted to integrate Forest into it so I don't have to access my phone whenever I wanted to use it. Forest's apple watch version only allows you to view how many trees you have planted and stats nothing more. The alternative I've thought of is to just use the Timer but it's not as effective at making me focus as Forest because it also blocks notifications from apps I pre-selected and it also plants virtual trees whenever I'm able to finish set time and wilts trees if I access my phone before set time.

I hope the Forest team is able to work on an update that would allow the feature I have mentioned above to work.

title: Great app for ADHD but i wish it had an alarm for completed focus times
body:
I give it 4 stars overall because it has helped with managing my productivity and inattention. It also keeps me motivated because focus time can lead to actual trees being planted and it makes simple things values- and advocacy-driven, which is a stronger motivation source for me than gamification, although the latter does help a lot also. I love seeing my forest at the end of each week. It is also very helpful that there is a timer mode and a set time mode and a switch to turn deep focus mode on and off because there are tasks that I need to switch apps like when I need to use the calculator app or check the calendar. 

I give it 4 stars because it is nearly perfect. I just wish it had the option to add a soothing alarm sound and congratulatory banner after each set focus time so I know when the time is up. One of my issues with ADHD is that hyperfocusing leads to obsession or lack of balance and it would be great to have a reminder at the end of 30 minutes or so to remind me to pause and check in with my energy. I can’t do this with the current app or ai just don’t know how? I’m new to this. Either way, I hope it can be a feature in the next update. And just the same, would definitely recommend the app. I think it is useful as is.

title: More Features.
body: Let me start first by saying that this app is beyond spectacular. It genuinely made a positive impact on how I managed my time efficiently, and productively. However, as a user I passionately believe that there are some needed features. These features include (1) syncing the plant mode between devices of the same account, and (2) allowing some apps to be exempt from the deep plant mode. The prior suggestion I just got from another review of the app, the latter I formed myself. I think we should be given the option to use 3rd party apps in deep focus mode that will not kill the plant. These apps are generally educational i.e. Notability, Goodnotes, Microsoft applications, et al. As a student using an iPad for primarily academic purposes, I truly believe these are necessary for the app to become better.

title: Do NOT purchase this app if you use your iPad
body:
Found this on the chrome extension first and it worked great. On the iPad though, not so much. iOS does not allow the app to monitor your app usage so you can’t blacklist/white list apps. It’s all or nothing if you use deep focus mode. Other than that, it doesn’t even support landscape mode. 

If you’re distracted by your phone/iPad, it’s a good app, but if you need those devices for work then look for something else.

title: This is app is very useful though I have some suggestions
body:
I love everything about this app especially that i could spend my coins for real trees. I give it 5 stars though I have some suggestions.

 Firstly, I think you could add some border to the circle of the tree that is planted, and it will serve as a visual to know where I am in my time(ex. the border of the circle is filled around 1/3 ,therefore I know that I still have 2/3 of the time). 

Another is the App Allow List, I’m an iOS user and it’s not yet available. I hope you can find a way to have it because I easily get distracted if I turn off the Deep Focus Mode and it isn’t as much fulfillment as to in Deep Focus Mode. 

Lastly, for the sounds there isn’t much of a variety. I hope that you’re going to add some classical music and lofi.

Thank you so much for this app! It’s totally worth it’s price! :))

title: simply life-changing.
body: This app is a simple and a useful means for productivity. Whenever I plant a tree or a bush or etc. I am always determined to not let the plant die because who doesn’t want a perfect streak with no withered plants? Whenever I feel like I spent way too much time on my phone, I just immediately go to the Forest app and plant to hinder me from using my phone any longer. I am much more encouraged as well to actually plant these plants that do not want me to use my phone because as I build up my coins, I can also help in the tree-planting project the Forest team is promoting and is also their advocacy. I have currently purchased 2 actual trees for the Forest team to plant and I can’t wait to purchase more actual trees! This app is very simple yet very useful for everyone trying to combat their phone addiction and finally live life outside our digital screens. My life has improved so much from the past few months with the help of this app and I have never regretted ever purchasing this app.

title: My best app purchase!
body:
By far my best app purchase. Highly recommend for those struggling to maintain focus on anything because of social media and their gadgets. I don’t usually review apps but this one totally deserves it. 

Basically the app lets you plant a virtual tree. Your tree dies if you use your gadget or open any other app. You get to track your gadget time too so you’re more aware of how much time you spend or waste (lol) on your phone. Really useful app!

Bonus: You get points for planting your virtual tree and unlocking achievements so that if you get 2,500 points you can plant a real tree!

I’m currently using quizlet to create virtual flashcards and I am as focused as I was before, but I only get half the coins since I use my phone to input information. :(

title: With a Little Honesty, You can Improve Performance Awareness and Work Efficiency
body: When you plant and track hours here, you can't open other apps or your plant will die. Therefore, zero activity on the phone. But you can still visit facebook, instagram, and other distracting sites using your other gadgets. That's the setback. That's why I said, you have to be honest by not visiting other non-related sites in your other gadgets while you track hours using this app on your phone. If you do this, you can view from this app the trees and bushes you planted and label them according to the task you were handling during these hours. By looking at your activity page in the app, you will see the work you've accomplished and the number of hours or minutes you spent on them. Great app if you'll only be honest!

title: What a joke
body: I almost never write reviews. But man do I feel like venting my frustrations out on this malicious app's setup. In general it works well enough, but after the first few times of using the app, it will ask you to sign up and by doing so steal your data, I mean give you gifts. I choose to continue as a guest and because of that I lost all of my coins and my forrest. Lmao, what a predatory system. basically, sign up or we will reset your progress every day. At first I liked the idea of this app  and I was even considering buying some of the seeds to support the developers but guess not. Honestly, perhaps I wouldn't even be writing this if the app only had warned me about losing my progress but nope, it didn't even have the shame to do that little. Seeing my coins go from hundreds to zero after pressing the guest option, evoked the imagery of some comedy show making fun of ridicules capitalist business practices.

title: Deep focus mode not working and no way to delete account!
body:
Have used this app for 20+ hours and twice it happened now that all my trees withered because apparently I went away from the app. 

The only thing I did, from a locked phone, go directly into the app and it said “better luck next time”.

I won’t use the app without deep focus mode since that remove the reason for this app. 

If you plan on using this app and need the motivation of your trees withering if you leave the app, don’t pay for this because it doesn’t work all the time. 

Hate working, feeling like I got things done and then check the time left and see the trees withered..

There is also no way to delete your information so if you care about your privacy, don’t create an account and maybe not use the app at all!

title: Great for someone with ADHD
body:
I love it! I think this app worth the money. I have ADHD and I use this at work and at home when I have to clean and do other boring tasks. It gets easier when I just set a timer for however long I need to be doing something. 25 min intervals is generally a good amount of time, so if you use the pomodoro technique you'll get one tree for every 25 minutes when you use this app. I always think it's hard to get started with tasks, and sometimes I usually start this app to make it easier to get in the right mindset, and make myself want to deserve a pretty forrest. So I start it evan if I can't focus at 100% to just have it as an habit. And I do think it helps at least with getting started, and sometimes staying on track as well when you see how little time is left and how much your tree has grown.

I just wish I had more friends who use it so we could follow each other and see each others progress. But using it by myself is also great since I mostly do it to motivate myself. So try this app if you need more motivation to get things done! And if you like it, buy it to support the creators of the app!

title: Game changer: Staying focused for the world’s forests
body: I normally never write app reviews, but I feel like this one has to shared with the world. I am so much more motivated to study and keep focused with this app. By setting the tree-timer to your preferred focus time, you grow a tree by not touching you phone in that time. If you do, your tree dies. Once you have grown a tree it show up in a little forrest. It is so satisfying seeing a little forest in front of you after a productive day! And killing a tree by flicking with your phone is really helpful to stay away from it.... What motivates me the most is that once you have grown enough focus-trees, you can plant a real tree. This makes me feel like I am studying for the world’s forests 🌱

title: Surprised!
body: The app is simple to use and handle. It has a pleasing and relaxed design that in itself has a stress reducing effect. It’s function follows the ‘Pomodoro’ concept and aim to keep you away from other things and focus on a particular task for a given space of time (that you choose yourself). This it does superbly because it gives you a little reward in form of a virtual planted tree for each uninterrupted time-space. Eventually you will build a lush forest. I am surprised how well this little rewarding-tweak functions... I really want that forest! I am not giving 5 stars since I would want the app to provide for an info badge (of time progress etc.) when the phone is in lock-mode, so till then it’s four stars. Nevertheless, to all of you in search of help to better do concentrated work... give this a try.

title: Positive Review and Suggestion
body:
Forest is an innovative application that creates a simple system in which productivity is "rewarded" in the application. I have no complaints and have been enjoying the application so far.

However, I would love it if Forest allows notification messages to be customised. Currently, the reminder only reminds to use Forest. I would love it if the notification can be personalised. For example, at noon the notification is set as "Continue with your assignments!" This allows the reminder to remind more than just the When but the What.

title: Became too profit driven, deleting the app
body:
Once an app gets too big, the app starts to lose focus of the app’s main purpose. That’s what happened to Forest. 

It used to be so straight forward, which is just to track your study time and you get a digital tree in your forest for studying. Now, it’s all about trying to make you buy coins, pop ups after pop ups, and trying to get you to get this type of tree and plant. It’s so silly to me. Do they not know the demographics of their users? 

Are people really paying for “coins”? And for what? JUST focus on studying and passing your class/exams. 

The last straw for me was the app removing the total focus  time of the day on the main screen. what?? That’s literally the whole point of a study app…. To track your total time spent studying. 

I know they see their growing user base and now all they think about is how to extract money from each of them. It’s literally just a study app.. what kind of big money do y’all really think you will eventually make? 

Farewell. I’ll be using another study app from now on.

title: Too much AI, which is a shame.
body: I bought forest a while ago and it really improved my study sessions. It’s genuinely an amazing app and I love that you can buy the customizations for free if you just focus enough and grow enough trees. I also think the in-game coins to real life trees system is amazing! If only you didn’t immediately kill those trees by promoting the use of AI. I stopped using the app a few years ago and picked it back up for college, and everything changed. The user interface is TERRIBLE. It’s slow when trying to go anywhere but the main planting menu. And when you are done with a session, you click like 5 times on a button that says go home. I clicked “Go home” already, let me go. Other people have tried emailing support with complaints about ads (since I was an early supporter, I get an ad free experience) and they got a fully generative AI response which included the AI thinking process, of which included the AI not furthering the request for a refund because the user said they “wished” they could request a refund instead of saying “I would like to request a refund.” It’s insane to me that a company who promotes trees and understands that people do, in fact, like trees, doesn’t understand that using AI to generate and manage your entire app is scummy. This company should be ashamed.

title: Retro User
body:
I first downloaded this app about 6 years ago and used it with a friend. We both loved it; it was a simple way to keep us both off our phones and on task. Each of us even bought a subscription. 

These past few months, the UI updates and AI integration have made this app so, so clunky. It breaks my heart to say that it's an eyesore now. The designs feel so much less simple and human-made. Clicking through a series of prompts makes the planting feature less efficient to use. 

Please, please offer some settings to help us go back to the way things were. Cut the AI garbage and cumbersome UI. For an app that espouses the value of getting off screen and going out into the world to do good (planting trees irl, getting your work done and be a functioning person), the AI integration is such a big disappointment.

title: Stop asking for money
body:

I have thousands of coins and absolutely nothing to spend them on because you’re only focusing on things for your subscription. And that’s after the shop got “fixed.” Which it didn’t, not really. You got rid of bundles, which I was saving for since they were a little discounted. You have to hope you’re lucky and get a gem tree that you want when you finally saved enough. Just stop. You’ve pushed so many people away from your app because you keep ruining it. You made it take so long just to get to the Home Screen after a session. My app glitched on me today and the alert that the session stopped and rewards came an hour after I stopped it. Please, for the love of God, stop making this app worse. Stop asking for money when people have already paid.

title: New UI Has Some Pros, But I Haaaaate the Popups
body:
They changed the user interface today. 

What I like:
- The new “my plants” section makes it easier to see trees.
- It’s easier to pick a tag.

What I don’t like:
- Annoying popups flash across my screen when I finish planting a tree and want to back to the home screen! This app is supposed to reduce distractions, not create them. 
- Some of the trees displayed are not purchasable in the store, yet clicking on them still takes me to the store. 
- There are still very few tag colors. Other people and I specifically submitted a feedback request asking for more tag colors, but there are still just a handful. 

What I feel mixed about:
- The trees bounce up and down, and the coin icon shimmers. It’s kind of cool, but also very distracting.



Edit; I changed my review to one star. They’re now deleting trees from the regular store and making you rebuy them for a much higher price only on certain days when they happen to appear in the temporary store that refreshes daily. This is so stupid. It’s clear that they’re creating a scarcity mindset to pressure people to check the app often. That goes against the whole point of making an app to get you off your phone!

title: Downhill Slide
body: I’ve used this app since 2016 and have been a huge advocate for it since early days. While I can’t think of any period of time in the past decade where the Forest app has maintained excellent stability free of glitches, the overall usefulness of the app has allowed me to look past that. In the past 12-18 months, things have been going downhill. The devs keep pushing out excessive updates that prioritize gamification in the app and focus on money-making capacity of the app. All the while, stability in the app for users like myself and my friends has decreased and glitches have increased to the point of a non-functional app. Sharing session links, planting together, and Deep Focus mode are all useless now with the rollout of a new UI and the retirement of “classic” mode. It’s a real shame. I’ve accumulated over 275 days of planting time in this app, the majority of which were logged in Plant Together mode with friends. I’ll be sad to leave the app and my land of virtual trees behind, but it may be the natural course of things if the devs continue to ignore prioritization of the function and stability of the Forest app.

title: I love this app, but…
body:
I really love this app. I’ve been using it for years and have found it very helpful to focus and track my writing time. However, since the introduction of focus challenge I have been annoyed by the implementation. My biggest issue is the fact that I have to reset my focus timer each time I want to “plant a tree” for the challenge. If I do 2 hours in the app, it says I planted 4 trees in my forest but only one tree for the daily challenge. If the daily challenge says “plant any tree 4 times” I have to start and stop my focus timer four times (once every 30 minutes) in order for the trees to count. Why? The fact that I have to interrupt my focus time to stop and reset in order to achieve the daily challenge is ridiculous. It’s actually the opposite of focus, enough that I may have to switch to a different app because it is distracting me trying to keep my trees and focus time to match. 

Please fix this. Make it so that when I focus for a number of hours, the daily challenge counts my trees planted, not by the number of times I started focusing. It feels like a bug, but it’s been present since the focus challenge released. Thanks!

title: New look and streamlined-ness kind of terrible, otherwise love it
body:
Been using this app for years and love it. Don’t seem to have the glitches every other review talks about. But they keep changing the look of the app, and where buttons are, and what direction you need to scroll to pick a tree or a focus title you have, and they do this like every 2-3 months it seems. It makes it feel extremely inconsistent, and when I’ve finally gotten the muscle memory down for the app to feel streamlined and easy to use and find everything in, they suddenly change all of it again, and it becomes frustrating. Pick a look that works and stick with it. Why change the look if it’s not broken? This most recent look/button/scrolling update is so bad it makes me not want to use the app. Everything got enlarged so huge, text runs off the edge of the menu. Buttons are huge, yet for any function I need to go through hoops of multiple buttons or menus, when before it was just one button or everything in one menu. I need to click stop, then collect reward, when before it just collected reward automatically no extra button press needed. Now I need to pick a focus and a tree in two separate menus, tap to enter tree select menu, tap to exit, tap to enter focus title menu, tap to exit. Before these things were in the same menu. What was two buttons to enter and then exit menu, is now 4, since it’s been split into two menus. The way to scroll through trees vertically instead of horizontally feels wrong…who thinks of trees as being stacked on top of each other? No one. It feels kind of unintuitive and unnatural. And now because text is huge, scrolling vertically to pick a focus title out of many that I have is just a hassle and very ugly looking. Maybe this works for people used to reading text vertically, and could be used in those regions, or an option to switch between one or the other for those who prefer that direction of reading, but scrolling vertically through theses feels unnatural to me as well. When reading my eyes want to move left to right, the way it was horizontally scrolling before. But now my brain has to stop and start and stop and start as it jumps up and down the vertical list. 
The extra buttons and menus, and the new scrolling format makes using the app take twice as much time as it did before, which is taking away from the time people want to be focusing on whatever they’re getting set up to focus on. It just feels like twice as much work to use the app now. And everything in the app seems extra large now, like I accidentally bought an extra large print book. I’m not sure who they were making this update for, but it feels like it is not for students or young adults anymore.

title: Previously great app, but new update is AWFUL
body:
I’m a daily user and the new update killed the entire flow I loved about Forest. It’s still a decent pomodoro timer but two of my main complaints:

1. there’s a straight up bug when you click on a “your tree just finished growing” notification. Half of the time, it just shows me my tree with the timer at 00:00, and a cancel button that does nothing. I have to quit the app fully and return for it to let me claim my focus time + rewards. This also loses any “count exceeded time” you’d accumulated. This is still unfixed like a week after the new update and it makes me want to just use a different app entirely.
2. You have to click through way too many prompts now. I miss the simple “your tree grew” notification. Now it’s “your tree finished” -> claim rewards -> return home, each with their own slow animation. This is a POMODORO TIMER, you’re not a video game loading an open world where you need loading screens and door opening animations for Christ’s sake, let me get on with my work.

I hope you improve the app, I’ll be exploring alternatives in the meantime.

title: Bloatware Garbage
body:
I’ve used this app from the beginning almost 10 years ago. Even got offers as the 1% user from the developer to test beta features… It used to be cool. 

Now, it’s turned into corporate, bloatedware garbage where planting a tree feels easier to do in real life than by navigating this app. Having derailed from its original mission of providing the user with a simple interface to increase digital productivity, it now does the complete opposite, feeding into the problem of the attention divided economy rather than helping solve it.

It’s just really sad to watch these original cool simple apps turn into confusing mazes of micro transaction pop ups, incessant updates which somehow make the app more buggy, and ever expanding side menus advertising products that have nothing to do with the original app purpose. 

After almost a decade of using this app I’m putting my forest to rest. I bought an actual tree and planted it and feel better for it, I suggest other users do the same.

title: Recommended by OT but not quite doing the job.
body:
I have AUDHD with some OCD, anxiety and exhaustion. I am dealing with physical disability as well from nervous system and autoimmune issues. I’m in occupational therapy for speech, physical rehab, and soon will be adding visual OT. My speech therapist thinks that the root of a lot of my problems is actually exhaustion from excessive screen time. My screen time has become an escape hatch from my preexisting issues, but it worsens them so it’s an endless feedback loop. We are using this app to try stepping down from my usage of social media in particular. 


Most of us have multiple devices. I have an iPad, MacBook, iPhone and Apple Watch and the app doesn’t automatically sync across these devices. It doesn’t automatically lock down all my devices, I have to grow a tree separately on each even after syncing them. 

It doesn’t reliably block access to apps when in focus mode. It says I’m in focus right now and I can access all my apps without killing my tree. 

I don’t like the stats board. I have premium and it is showing me whatever I’ve tagged my usage as, instead of using existing Apple analytics to populate that chart. Rocket money and Mint seem to be able to create good pie charts and graphs based off access to account info, so wondering why this isn’t the same. 

I find the current description key for the charts comparing one day against another a bit vague. More concise wording is needed to provide a key to understanding that one. Is this even a helpful metric? Why not something more simple and engaging like “wow, you did it! Your break from screens lasted 20% longer than yesterday, with a total of 4.5 hours!” The way it’s set up now is very flat and boring and tbh hard to tell if it’s a positive or negative comparison. 

The daily challenge always has one goal I can’t meet without cashing in all my coins on a plant I don’t have to unlock it. Not a fan of that as a premium user. 

I did like being able to set focus to run from a set time in morning to a set time in evening. I didn’t like that it doesn’t automatically remember this setting and do it every day Monday through Friday (or whatever you prefer). It did it well for my first day, and then wasn’t in place the next morning. I really need the features to run for consecutive days in order for this to work. Relying on me to remember or have the willpower to do this every day in the beginning is not helpful. I have adhd, this is not accounting for how our disability shows up. We are more prone to addiction to screens, and have more difficulty creating new habits, especially when the new habit is in conflict with an established maladaptive ritual. A setting where I can explain what level assistance I need, and then consent to a time frame or schedule for the week/month would work better than what it’s doing now. 


I’d love to see a journal of symptoms and encouragement/coping strategies  included in the app. Other addiction apps provide structured support for the hard parts of cycle breaking. Since I’m doing this on the recommendation of a doctor, would be cool to be able to log symptoms and share that kind of chart with them over time. To view my progress that way. 
For example, I experienced a lot of anxiety and agitation my first day. I had observations about my energy levels, and would like to have stored what I did with my time instead on the app for a productivity chart or something. I also experienced insomnia my first night, and would have benefitted from charting that, sleep as a metric is useful, and possibly links to resources to help fall asleep. 


I hate the “take a break” options. The breathing animation and “peaceful sounds” are awful. They’re loud and distracting, and without sound pretty useless. The breathing is way too fast for calming down. 

And last, I much prefer setting up the app to block my access to specific things for a set time period, vs checking it every 20 minutes or so to get a tree. Why cant we still get trees and coins for the time we are in deep focus for hours? I get ONE tree no matter how long the break is. Repeatedly checking the app is defeating the purpose of staying off the device. Picking it up to do that makes me want to check social media. I’m trying to wean off the default of looking at my phone during my more functional hours when I should be doing IRL things.

title: REALLY dislike the new UI
body:
I really miss the radial time select, and I hate that my trees are no longer ordered by last used. I used to cycle through plants, choosing the one I haven’t chosen before in the longest amount of time, to keep my forest a balanced mix of species. Now, even when trying to sort by recently used, it’s not giving me that actual list, because I know some of them that should be close together that aren’t. I would like the radial time back instead of having to click through another menu, and I’d like an actual list organized by the order I’ve selected plants in.

I don’t understand why this app (which at its best has been great!!) feels the need to keep reinventing itself without any seeming regard for actual user experience — it feels like someone’s just got it in their head that they NEED to switch things up regularly. 

Given the app developer’s propensity for AI, in both their chatGPT developer responses and their other AI app, I’m wondering if at an upper level, someone is prompting an AI for ideas and then implementing them because AI said so. I don’t entirely trust that these are human-led poor decisions, just because some of them are SO baffling (literally why would you change the dial function to a pop up menu?? that’s more clicks and you can’t easily see what the plant looks like at each time any more. Any designer should have been able to point to that as an unnecessary change, and I KNOW this app has at least utilized qualified designers in the past, because it looked great before you changed it!)

title: Excellent app, esp. with a couple more features
body:
This is an excellent app. I didn’t think the gamified focus system would do much for me, but surprisingly, it does. Not wanting your tree to wither is a real motivator for me lol and the visual reward of all the different plants is surprisingly helpful. I thought a simpler pomodoro app would be my go to but I think it’s going to end up being this one! 

That said, a couple things would really make this a 10/10 for me: 
- allow starting a session/break on watch - I know there is an issue with blocking phone apps this way, but personally I’d be happy to not have them blocked and still have this feature!
- allow break timer to show on watch - esp. helpful for longer breaks 
- show session timer in watch app, not just complication (caveat: one issue with 9/10 timer apps is that the alert won’t go off when the app is open - please allow it to stay on as watch raise to wake feature leads to missed alerts this way) 
- allow us to set a break timer not just from the session end screen 

Thank you so much for this app it’s truly a blessing!

title: Shout out to the Forest team for caring about user satisfaction! 💯
body:
I’m really impressed by how quickly the team addressed the issues I mentioned in a previous review (they were fixed within hours).

In that review, I also suggested bringing back more flexibility with pauses, since some users need short breaks when they notice their attention starting to fade. Being able to pause when needed makes it easier to stay focused during longer sessions and helps Forest better support users who have difficulty concentrating for extended periods.

The app is great as it is, in my opinion, but to better accommodate different users’ needs and study styles without making it too tempting to pause constantly, one suggestion would be to add a setting that lets users toggle between one pause per session and unlimited pauses. Giving users the option to choose their preferred pause setting would make Forest more flexible and supportive for different attention spans and routines.

Overall, I really enjoy Forest and value that the developers listen to user feedback. Thank you for continuing to improve Forest and for creating a functional platform that helps us stay focused and reach our goals.

title: Это невероятно
body: Помимо того, что приложение имеет серьезное проблемы с уведомлениями, из за которых ты не контролируешь окончание цикла и активацию нового. Вечером приходится буквально сидеть и считать через вкладку «история» время и складывать вручную. После покупки Forest Plus, приложение стало просто фантастически непредсказуемо себя вести. Уведомления приходят случайным образом в разное время в течение активированного цикла по несколько раз. А запущенные циклы на 180 минут потом в конечном итоге показывают во вкладке «история» совершенно другие, ложные! В моем случае это были 8 минут и 12, без прерываний, что уже невозможно! Нет таких опций при выборе времени запуска цикла. В итоге окончательное время в конце рабочего/учебного дня критично разнится с реальными затраченными часами сосредоточенности. Это невероятно, нет слов. Приложение - вакханалия и дилетантство. Так же, иногда приложение само запускает цикл на 30 минут. Вопрос, что с вами не так. Не рекомендую. Не тратьте время и нервы. Это очень сильно раздражает и выводит из себя.хотите стать нервным, вперед!

title: Mis-taps & a Hassle to Exit + No Shortcut Support
body:
Originally, after planting a tree, the Rest button was the most prominent at the bottom, making it simple to end the session, and back to main screen. Now Forest has replaced this with its Rest & Breathing Timer, since that button is still the most prominent one on the screen, it’s way too easy to mis-tap by accident. To make it even more frustrating, you have to long-press just to exit the Rest & Breathing Timer once you’ve mis-tapped it, which is such a counterintuitive, annoying design.

What’s more, I really dislike that Forest requires you to open the app directly for all actions. I much prefer launching focus timers via Shortcuts, as it lets me start a session without any distractions. If Forest won’t add support for Shortcuts for a seamless start, it should at the very least polish the basic in-app experience—but this forced update only ruins it with poor design choices.

title: Features I PAID for were removed
body:
I’m really upset because about two months after I paid to download this app, multiple core features were removed and are now locked behind a monthly subscription.

I have no issue with the app introducing a subscription for additional features. The problem is that I specifically paid for this app with the understanding that these features were included. Removing functionality that paying users already purchased feels lazy and scummy, especially when the alternative would be to simply add new premium features instead.

Some features that were removed include:
	•	The ability to choose which apps are blocked during a focus period
	•	Viewing detailed focus stats (such as which days and times you focus most)
	•	Creating and editing custom tags to label and group study sessions

On top of this, ads were added, and the app constantly pushes the subscription.

I genuinely enjoyed this app and found it helpful, but it has now become a source of frustration. All I’m asking is that the features I paid for be returned, and that subscriptions enhance the experience for subscribers rather than restrict it for everyone else.

The order of days, hours, weeks, and months appears to be reversed.

	•	Monday is displayed as Friday
	•	Similarly, the months are reversed:
	•	Month 1 is shown as 12
	•	Month 2 is shown as 11, and so on.

It seems that the calendar/time indexing is inverted, which causes incorrect labeling of days and months.

I would appreciate it if you could look into this issue and fix the reversed sequence.

title: Great app but could be even better
body: I love this app and use it daily, but there is one issue I have with it. Currently, to grow your tree fully, you need to set your focus time for 120 minutes. But, research shows the importance of not sitting in one spot that long and true focus is optimized in shorter bursts of time. So, those of us who set our focus time to less than 120 min never get fully-grown trees. There should be a way that offsets that default if you continue to build your tree, but in smaller time periods. As long as you select the same tree after each break, it would continue to grow until it is complete. That way, you are getting the full perks of focusing and still doing it in a healthy and optimal way.

title: This Changes Everything
body:
As someone who has always struggled with attention for repetitive or boring work tasks (paperwork, documentation, etc.) This has been a godsend. I was racking up way too much work time watching YT Shorts or TikTok, not because I wanted to, but because I’d get sucked into the vortex anytime I picked up my phone.

Well no more! I’ve enabled Deep Focus and locked out virtually every app that could distract me, and having something that depends on me staying focused completely reshaped my relationship with these tasks. 

I now WANT to spend time on them so I can keep growing trees and earning coins. I know gamification doesn’t work for a lot of people, but as a life-long millennial gamer, it has become an essential feature of any app I purchase. It keeps enabling me to stick to things I normally would’ve given up on in a few days (just passed one year of daily German lessons via Duolingo and now Busuu). If gamification works for you too, then just stop reading and buy the app already! 

The reason I dinged a star is due to how many microtransactions the app contains. I get it, it’s one of the only profitable ways to sustain an app company, but it feels like it’s nudging you to spend or buy on every page of the app except for study time. Even then, it’ll remind you how you could be getting 3x the coins if you sign up for Plus. Keep in mind, you have to pay $4 to use this app, making it a premium purchase. I get plastering that stuff everywhere when you offer a free membership option, but that’s not the case here. If the company is struggling to make ends meet, then start charging more, but whatever you do, lighten up on the gacha mechanics. Not saying they need to go, just that they shouldn’t be up in my face on every window.

title: Thanks!!!
body:
I’ve tried several apps to help me stay focused while studying, but Forest is the only one that truly transformed how I learn. As someone who used to struggle with attention and often felt frustrated for not “giving my all,” Forest helped me turn my perfectionism into a healthy motivation.

The ability to “plant trees” that grow based on how long I stay focused pushes me to beat my own record every day, and that has boosted my productivity like nothing else. Now I can maintain long study sessions (7 to 8 hours or more in a day) with steady focus that used to feel impossible.

Plus, seeing my progress visually reflected in a growing forest gives me a real, tangible sense of achievement. Forest has helped me not only study faster but also process and digest information better, moving past the anxiety of immediate perfection to focus on steady progress.

For anyone struggling with concentration or motivation, Forest isn’t just an app—it’s a companion that helps you reprogram your mind and build habits that actually work.

Suggestions: I would love to see a widget for iPhone standby mode to make tracking even easier. Also, giving users more opportunities to earn or buy trees would be awesome—because who wouldn’t want a bigger, greener forest?

title: I feel like I can’t complain about the App’s actual problems bc the basic concept is so effective
body:
I own two physical pomodoro timers. They were more expensive than this app and this app is way more effective. I really thought it wouldn’t work after I’ve tried everything to help my screen time problem only to weasel around them and eventually go back to my old ways. This app is amazing because it actually:
1- locks you out of distracting apps
2- guilt trips you if you try to weasel around it in a way that’s more effective than other guilt trip methods (think Duolingo’s reminders). If you give up, your plants die. And I don’t want my plants to die :(
3- you get an awesome visual representation of how long you’ve focused in a day unlike conventional pomodoro timers, which is really motivating
However, the pricing of the plants and the events leave something to be desired.
I don’t mind how long it takes to accumulate coins, it fits right in with the app’s “you reap what you sow, so work hard” ethos.
However, there’s so many missed opportunities for the game-like nature of the app. 
For starters there’s so many awesome limited-time plants you just can’t get if you join the app now because they’re not made available in the time crystal shop. And the plants that are in the time crystal shop are mostly seasonal holiday-themed decorations I have no interest in. So there’s this whole in-game currency that’s useless to me, and it could so easily become useful to me if the developers put more limited-time plants in the time crystal shop
There are also accomplishments/awards for focusing x number of hours that will gift you x number of coins for completing them. I think there should be more of these accomplishments because after a certain point you complete them all and it takes some of the freshness out of the game for people who have been playing longer. I think some new accomplishments could be awards for completing sets of plants. For example, in the shop there are plants that can be categorized together like fruit trees, plants indigenous to Africa and Asia, and tropical plants. If collecting all the plants in these groups came with an achievement and coin reward, it could be motivating for long-time players to collect more plants.
I like the monthly challenge, I think that’s great and they should never take it out.

title: Dislike the “Pay-to-Play”
body: The concept behind these focus apps is to hijack our brain’s reward systems to be productive rather than distracting. You get dopamine from focusing and getting a tree planted. But when the “reward” (planting a tree, unlocking trees, etc) becomes the goal in itself, then the app becomes a distraction in itself.  The first time I stopped using this app, I stopped because I had become obsessed with growing a beautiful forest. I notice there’s a lot of “pay-to-play” that takes advantage of this misdirected reward system, where you can pay to get more coins or diamonds to get more rewards. It would be good if these options were not so visible on the app and could be turned off and only accessible in the settings. This takes advantage of our brain’s reward systems for the developers’ profit rather than helping us direct it towards becoming productive.
