title: Great for studying
body: Honestly, I’m the type of person who just suddenly goes on my phone or laptop in the middle of doing homework, projects, etc. It’s especially been a problem since this new school year started. This app has helped me quite a lot, though sometimes I forget to plant a tree before I begin completing assignments. It’s helped with decreasing the amount of time I spend on schoolwork, and makes me feel like I’m doing so much more. Whenever I do reach over to my phone and am about to do something besides studying, like scrolling through Instagram, I’d open it and see the tree on my screen. Then, I’d ask myself, “Do I really want the tree to die?” I’d say no. In the beginning of using this app, I was always close to using my phone while the tree is growing. I began to develop a mentality after a few days that I should finish my homework before going on my phone and do other things. Of course, I sometimes still do it when I don’t use Forest, but I feel as if I’ve lessened the amount. This is the first productivity app I’ve used, and I’ve always seen people recommend it. It’s definitely an app worth the money. You can use it on your laptop or computer as well, as a Chrome extension (which is what I started out with). It’s simple to use, and has a minimalistic aesthetic that I really enjoy. Overall, it’s a great app.

author: Jeff Huhn

title: DONT BE HARD ON YOURSELF
body:
This is a WARNING: you do not do as much work as you think. LOL. 
Before I first started using a timer I was, in comparison to my teammates and age group (‘97 baby woot), what I thought, very productive. I don’t even remember the last time I was “late” for a deliverable or anything... I just wanted to organize my brain with a timer. 
OMG. The first day or two... phew. I felt DUMB. My total work time was maybe 2 hours. (Then I started wondering what the heck my teammates we doing all day, if they don’t even work that long, but whatever.)
Breaking everything down into tiny steps? Used to that. That’s business, baby. 
Breaking everything into 15-45 min tasks?Mind-altering. 
I usually stick to 20 or 25 with 5 min break after. That sounded counterproductive to me at first, but HA. I can genuinely say after using this app that I did not truly know what it was like to focus on one task for even 10 minutes. 

Tip: Start on and ALWAYS stick to deep work mode. This will give you the discipline you are most likely looking for. Trust me, it makes you very sad to see that dead tree.

title: Not Awesome on iPad
body:
As a time-tracking/management app, Forest is both easy to use and fun to engage with. That said, it’s clearly optimized for the iPhone. The iPad version doesn’t support landscape mode, which makes it rather awkward to use while working on an iPad. It’s a shame, since the increased real estate on a tablet offers a wealth of opportunity for, say, streamlining the information gathered by the app.

I also wish there were a pomodoro mode. Yes, I could try to kluge together a series of trees to approximate the pomodoro timer, but it’s a pain to figure out if it’s time for a long break and it’s too easy to remember not to start a break timer.

title: So close to perfect!
body:
I’ve used Forest for about a year now, and I love it on my IPhone! Before using Forest, I would find myself using my phone while studying, which would lead me to losing focus and having to reread sections of text because of that lack of focus. When I got this app, however, I started studying much more effectively because the urge to use my phone was no longer there. I would highly recommend this app to anyone who is having difficulty with staying focused!

Now as to ways that Forest can improve the app: I recently bought the Apple Watch SE, and when I saw that forest was available for my watch, I knew I had to download it! When I opened it up, however, I was greatly disappointed. You can’t start a study session on your Watch, and the majority (if not all) of the features that make Forest for the IPhone great aren’t present. To me, it would make sense to add the ability to set a study session on your watch and have the countdown on it. After all, isn’t Forest meant to keep you off your phone? I could over look this, if it weren’t for the fact that you pay for this app. Other apps similar to Forest have the same features on the Watch app and their IPhone app. On top of the superior functionality, some of those apps also have the benefit of being free. 

So to sum up: this app is amazing if you’re using it on your IPhone, but where it can truly shine (in my opinion) is the Apple Watch. Forest is an amazing app, and I truly hope that the developers find a way to add more features to their Apple Watch app.

title: Amazing.
body:
I only have two suggestions that could make this better aside from prettier trees.
1) the option to arrange the week’s forest like a garden. More than the week would obviously cause one to spend too much time on their phone.
2) THE IMPORTANT ONE: I wish I could automatically plant a tree at certain times of the day. I would love to get an alarm warning that I am planting a tree so I would have to open the app. I believe I would use it 6xs a day. I would have it set to plant a tree an hour before bed, for an hour shortly after my sleeptown alarm goes off, when it is time to make food, and for a meditation/prayer/edification break. Sometimes I forget to even use forest if I get really locked in or obsessive about something. I need the help.

I am a writer and I prefer working on a computer or device. I also have Hashimoto’s which causes a number of mental illnesses when mu hormones get messed up, like OCD, ADHD and anxiety. Obviously I know how to spend lots of time on something fairly simple. I have a couple friends I text too much too. Point being, it’s really easy for me to spend my entire day looking at my phone and it doesn’t leave me feeling good and I tend to neglect my body. 

This app has been pretty great. I didn’t like the tree I started with, though the final incarnation is okay lol. I do wish they all looked a little prettier. I like things less cartoony, and I don’t actually like evidence of people in it lol. But it’s fun to build a forest and it helps when I am conscious enough to think, “I need to pay attention to my kid right now.” Often I end up not even picking up my phone again for a long time after I put it down.

Lastly, it does allow for a couple seconds away which is good because I do like to listen to music or podcasts while I do stuff sometimes.

title: 简单·有用
body:
Forest优点非常明显：
a.自动化程度高。所有番茄开始和结束的时间都自动记录，便于回顾时观察自己休息时间长短，以及高效工作时长与时间段。
b.color code和标签是很好的任务记录符号。
c.番茄结束后，可以写下工作记录。
d.无需纸笔，节省空间。

有朋友提到为了减少手机使用，他避免用Forest。这个问题完全可以得到改进。我有一个退休的iPhone SE，上面只安装了Forest。这样就算用手机，也不用担心短信和电话的干扰。现在便宜手机很多，完全可以用起来。

title: Make landscape, split view, and slide over view
body: I love this app, but it’s shocking that after years there is still NO support for landscape view, split view, and slide over view. Absolutely not ok for a 5 star rating. I take notes in landscape view a lot as a lot of people do, and it’s frustrating to have to go back to portrait view because forest does not support landscape view. While it’s a small annoyance of rotating my iPad 90 degrees every time I use forest, the annoyance grows overtime hence why I’m writing this lengthy review. I should be able to switch between my note taking app and still be in landscape mode after going to forest. I should be able to use slide over I can get a peek of the time I have left to focus while studying. But instead I have to rotate my iPad making some resistance to my workflow.

body: Love this app so much! In the beginning, I didn’t think it would help as much as it does now. With the deep focus mode, I can still listen to Spotify music but it prohibits me from actually leaving the app, or else the tree will die. The app provides study music like rainforest sounds, and you can buy nice trees and more sounds from coins earned from focusing. This is a really great method that rewards you with something positive, and even displays your focus progress over a day/week/month. As a chronic procrastinator, this is helping me fix bad habits like constantly checking texts, apps, or getting distracted by YouTube videos.

title: College Procrastination
body:
Thanks to COVID, all my freshman college courses are online, and procrastination has been the devil on my shoulder. 

This app has helped me eliminate my procrastination, and I didn’t realize how much my cellphone was distracting me. The feature of “deep study mode” kills the tree you’re attempting to grow if you leave the app, and the stress of accidentally leaving the app is surprisingly immaculate. I spend less time thinking about going on social media, and more time focusing on growing my tree. 

It’s also allowed me to grow the tree, and reward myself further with a timed break the app suggests. 

This is the first review I’ve ever typed, I get a sea coral tree from typing a review, I’m pumped.

title: Not worth it.
body:
I usually never pay for apps but I thought this one would be helpful. I was wrong. I love how it plants trees in real life but it doesn’t help much with productivity. It’s mostly just a way of setting time and measuring progress. 

This app does not let me know when to stop. It is not ideal for studying. It would have been great if this app was more of a timer so I would know when to stop instead of checking my phone to know if the time is up. It can send alerts for when the tree is planted or when the time is done but so can my other apps, which is distracting. If I let this app notify me with sounds, I would also be letting other apps do the same. It would be inconvenient if I turned off notifications for other apps. 

The app has an option that prevents me from checking other apps while the time is running but the system is not ideal. I would still need to do the work; control myself. I could still open other apps but my tree would die. It would have been great if I couldn’t access non essential apps while trying to focus. 

Basically, I don’t need this app.

Does my payment for the app help plant trees? If it does, I’d feel less bad.

title: Practical. Some limitations due to iOS.
body:
This app is a godsend. Well... not really, but it feels better to say that than to admit “I have no discipline” or “I’m addicted to my phone.”

It is super helpful in establishing some self-parenting/boundaries with my stuff. Hopefully this has a spillover effect on my social media use.

The only complaint I have is that I can’t give certain apps permission to not interfere with the growth of my trees. That’s due to iOS and it seems like the developers are aware of the situation. I make up that the response is “that’s just the way it is, nobody likes it, but we all have to deal with it.”

The way it’s currently set up is: I either pick the Deep-Focus mode that harms my growth if I exit the app or cancel the D-F mode, which means I can go in and out of the app. Basically all-or-nothing, which blows for my particular setup because I do use some apps for legitimate work reasons. I’ll have to find a way around that for now.

4/5 would recommend. If this Deep-Focus thing ever gets resolved, I’ll change it to 5/5.

title: Needs some work
body:
I’ve rated this app 3 stars.  It does the job and looks nice and friendly but... 

1) Please add landscape mode - if it’s available, I haven’t found it.  This is my biggest grip by far.  

2) The unlocking and gamification could definitely use a lot of love.  I know this isn’t the crux of what the app does but penalizing me for canceling a session by charging 60 coins seems too penalizing.  Earning coins takes too long.  The ‘reward’ of seeing the variety of the forest is meh...  

This could really be a killer app if these two things were added... I better get back to work :-)

title: Such a good app for productive sessions.
body:
I’ve been using the app since around 2018 I think? 

It has been a go-to for when I need to sanction time out of my day to do work, be productive, so on. 

The concept is fun and the app has a nice UI. It has looked great for a long time. I love the new widget options and versatility of all 6 types - honestly one of the best new widgets out there, I’d say. 

Every thing about it is clean and simple, while promoting productivity.

My only suggestion would be the ability to start planting from the Apple Watch app (synced to the iOS app). To me, being able to only see my forest on the watch app is kind of useless.

Great app all around. Would recommend it to anyone!

title: Love my forest!
body:
I know. The app seems silly. My friends laugh at me. I understand. But for those that are serious about limiting screen time, it is a HUGE HELP. For some perspective, I averaged 7.5 HOURS A DAY on my phone! That’s insane. I work in the media, so I’m naturally on my phone a lot but I need to be more in the present moment and unplug. 

This app does exactly that with a fun little game/challenge included when it comes to building your forest. The more lush the better!

Give it a try but only if you’re actually serious about changing your bad screen time habit. I did, and now I’ve cut off 3 hours! Within a single week!

title: Challenging App to Inspire a New Level if Focus
body: Planting trees requires REAL work. 1 simple timer won’t cut it and that’s where your role begins. You have the chance to push yourself to new levels of concentration to save as many coins as you can to plant a real tree at 2,500 coins. 2,500 coins is a daunting challenge that isn’t cut out for everyone. Be the exception. Be better than yourself. The more you study, the closer you get to adding real trees to the world. I thought I’d genuinely be planting at least 1 tree a day. Although I originally thought this was too good to be true, it is very clear the challenge you are presented with to create a better environment. Join the wave and enjoy the benefits of the new you. See ya there.

title: Such a useful app
body:
My first app review...here we go!
This has to be one of my favorite apps. I take some pretty advanced classes and it’s important that I get the focus time I need. This app does an amazing job at encouraging me to not only stay off of social media apps, but to actually want to use this app to rack up coins and study time. You get coins for using the timer, and once you finish, you can spend them in the virtual store. It’s so satisfying to be able to earn new study sounds and/or trees to plant. Ah- forgot about that. While you focus, a virtual tree is planted and grows until you finish. It’s then added to your personal virtual garden- and I make a daily goal to make it as pretty as possible! Also you can use the coins you earn to have a real life tree planted somewhere In the world! Imagine getting work done AND saving the environment? Killing two birds with one productive app!

title: Fun and works, but needs more features
body: So far I’m actively using it and having fun with it. I do feel more rewarded and accomplished when I finish a task which makes studying more fun and working from home less of a chore. It was definitely worth the $2! I think a reading feature would help though, especially for studying. It operates strictly on a timer, but say you need to read two chapters before tomorrow. It’s really hard to tell how long that will take. If you take to the material easily, it won’t take nearly as long as you expected to finish but if you stop the timer early you don’t get rewarded. So a checklist or task feature that maybe worked it conjunction with the timer would be better, something where you could mark a task as completed without being pinged because you got it done quicker than you thought. This could also work well if you’re trying to get chores done without getting distracted. Right now, this is better for work or sleep when you know you’re only going to be doing it for a set amount of time.

title: i enjoy it, but i’m missing some things
body:
i really like using this app to track how much time i spend on my work and it helps to take breaks with timed sessions so you avoid burning out. i like the tagging system so you can see specially how much time you spend on a certain task, such as certain classes or chores. i like that it shows which days you’re most productive and other interesting stats, and you can plant actual trees after awhile. 

some features i wish were included would be the ability to add a tree/chunk of time for the times i do work and forget to set the timer. id also like to be able to set a stopwatch without an ending because sometimes i want to keep working past the original time set. it’s annoying to have to pick it up and set an extra 10-15 minutes. at the same time, sometimes i’ll finish my work sooner than when the timer goes off, and then i need to kill the tree i’m currently growing or just let the timer finish, but then my times are slightly inaccurate. i know this is nitpicky, but it’s just some features i’ve used with other apps that i really enjoyed. i will continue to use this app regardless because i like their commitment to helping the environment and i think the forests are cute ways of tracking time spent.

title: Faulty Chrome extension
body:
This app used to be great, and its strongest point is the syncing between web browser and mobile app. While the mobile app still gets regular updates, the Chrome extension is no longer maintained. It stopped working in 2019 and was never updated. Trees planted in Chrome sessions are not synced, and the extension is really glitchy. Most of the distractions in WFH comes from web browsing. Developers, please fix the Chrome extension.

EDIT: Devs got in touch to say the Chrome extension was updated. Well, it was not. Everything is still buggy. The screen is not responsive unless you close it and open again. Can't change tree species. Won't sync. Doesn't work at all.

title: Helpful & Fun!
body: I love this app! However, I hardly used it when I was actually in school (because the lazy student I was raced through my studies so I could watch YouTube or play Roblox). At the start of the summer, I wanted to stay productive (because even though I rushed through my work, I’m a huge nerd that likes school), so I decided to learn Spanish. I didn’t use Forest while I was learning Spanish because I completely forgot about the app. Eventually, I got tired of Spanish (and of course duolingo shamed me for it), and so I’m trying to learn Japanese. Japanese is a big struggle, and that’s when I remembered I had this app. This app is very helpful, because I can stay on track instead of getting bored and picking up my phone. My grades in school last year were terrible and I was on the verge of being dropped from advanced classes, but my grades improved when I started studying, despite rushing through my studies. This upcoming year, I hope that I’ll be able to use this app more. Also, because I’m doing virtual learning, I’ll get more chances to use this app! 🤗 さよなら!

title: Helps me be more productive
body:
This has been a great find for me. I set it like a pomodoro timer, 25 minutes at a time. I’ve been getting a lot of writing down, as well as getting work done on some other goals. Now, you can definitely “cheat”, so to speak, but like my teachers back in grade school would say, “you’re only cheating yourself”. 
Thing is, you might want to use your phone for the task you are working on. I like writing on my phone over paper and pen and even my laptop. So you can set the app to allow you to grow your tree even when you’re not in the app itself. And that’s how one could “cheat”. 
But I highly recommend the app. It’s been a fantastic help in me being more productive lately.

title: Useful, helpful, needs some improvements...
body:
Thank you for Forest. I appreciate the motivation the app creates to stay focused.

Several things are bothersome. I’m a tablet user, and I have an attached keyboard. It is not helpful to be limited to portrait view only. That’s kind of primitive, like early 2000s. Please add landscape view.

Second, it seems counterintuitive to have a support page that requires you to scan the page you are looking at to get to FAQs. Scan with what? Another device? Why would you assume I would have two devices? I suppose I can figure out a way to screenshot and then use it to get to support, but that’s not the solution I would expect from a Stanford guy.

Also, the Contact Us link do not create an email or go to a support fill-in form. It does nothing. So, you get to read my support request here. Please fix that.

I also found the app a little hard to work with at the start. The flow from operation to setup to reports to settings were not very easy to navigate. I still have some difficulty with this, and I think this can be improved.

Thank you for the productivity improvement that Forest brings. Keep upping the good work.

Otherwise, very well done.

title: Eric
body: I usually don’t write reviews, but I knew I had to write one for this app. At first, I had doubt. I’m they guy who constantly checks his phone for no reason and gets distracted. I planted the first tree, and magically, it just worked. I did longer trees and it helped me get off my phone for the whole night! The app makes you plant a tree, and you can’t exit the app for however long you set it. If you finish planting the tree, it goes in your forest. However, if you leave the app, the tree withers and shows up on your forest as well. You can use this with friends, coop, and gain coins for ever tree planted and achievement completed. Not only that, it is a relaxing app that has a selection of calming music(beach sounds, forest, etc). I believe the reason that this work is psychology. It makes you want to finish the tree and get coins, any brag you your friends about how many trees you planted. It puts pressure on you to not give up which I think is genius. Overall, this is probably one of my best purchases ever.

title: Need to have the ability to re-adjust time
body:
This app is very, very great. Definitely 5/5 stars to the majority of people. But, 3/5 stars for me.

I want the ability to re-adjust each time spent on focusing. 

For example: I enabled “count exceeded time” in the app setting and used 30 mins timer for studying. Then after studying for only 30 minutes, I forgot to stop the timer and, instead, went 50+ minutes rather than 30 mins. This ruins the accuracy of my tracked time. 

Perhaps take back my 1 coin for every 6 min re-adjustment.

I feel a pang of guilt when I pick up my phone and deviate from the forest telling me that my tree/s will die if I quit focusing LOL it’s actually been extremely helpful for me to keep track of my study time, I never realized how often I am distracted by notifications, text messages, etc, and Forest has helped me stay on track in the most interesting and beautiful way. title: One of the best apps I’ve ever purchased
body:
Here’s the truth: I’m only in middle school but this app has been a LIFESAVER. I’m a straight A student but still find myself procrastinating and not putting all my attention toward my schoolwork. Especially when I have an exam, I always wait till the last minute to study. Ever since getting this app though, I have found myself being more productive. This app allows me to set a goal for myself for when I would like to get something done in a period of time but still allows be to do it correctly. It makes you want to get your work done because you are building a forest while spending time towards your responsibilities. I have stopped looking at my phone every five seconds and have learned to detach from social media. This app has helped me pick up a good work ethic which is very much needed right now as I am having to start to prepare for high school.

If your anything like me, you have to have some sort of sound going on in the background. One specific thing I absolutely love about this app is it’s option to put on a sound while the timer is going. These sounds are soothing and don’t distract you. One sound for example, is just the background noise of a rainforest. I use this option all the time when doing homework or even just preparing for an exam. One thing I will have to say about this app is that your forest doesn’t grow very quickly. You have to be constantly using this app to fill up your forest and don’t get many plant options at first. But every time you grow a tree it’s very rewarding to see how your forest grows. Overall, I am so glad I stumbled upon this app and know I will continue to use this in the future. ( If your deciding whether or not to buy this app, I suggest you do. It’s well worth the two dollars. )

title: 100% Worthy Investment
body: I do not buy apps. Ever. It is against my religion. However, there was a quiz made by this app going around Twitter that told people what kind of plant they were. It was Pure™, so I looked into the app itself. When you need to get something done, you just set the timer and start planting a tree. I am an AWFUL procrastinator. I am procrastinating right now by writing this review. I can rarely be successfully guilted into not procrastinating. But when you leave this app, the tree you planted starts to die. Nothing has ever motivated me to stay off my phone more than a pixelated tree’s life in my hands. The app will even play soothing music while your tree grows. Everything about the aesthetic of this app is amazing and it actually works, if you find yourself saying “I’ll just text this person back really quick” then end up scrolling Twitter 30 minutes later. PLUS you can help plant real trees. 10/10 a great app, definitely worth the $1.99.

I am in the field of applied behavior analysis.

title: It's a neat app
body:
I have a hard time doing work because I easily get distracted but this app is certainly helping. I don't know how but I guess it's just how the app makes me consider that giving up on my task kills tree motivates me to keep going. The app also has features like being able to adjust the timer from 10 minutes to 2 hours of studying, get different kinds of trees, use gained coins to plant actual trees, has different kinds of study sounds, and my favorite is the deep focus mode where you can't leave the app at all. 

While I can force myself to focus on my own, this app makes it way easier to focus and makes it fun in an endearing way. And while they have lots of types of trees, I wish they had more kinds of study sounds and trees though.

title: allow the team to continue another plant task
body:
Hi forest developers, 

I am an addicted user and I love this apps very much. I urge you to propose a new function. That is to allow the team members to continue another plant task after the previous task is done. Currently, when the plan task is done, the team is disbanded. It’s very inconvenient to reorganize another team with previous team members if they were not the host’s friends. I strongly recommend you fixing this and allowing the host to commit another plant task with the last team members.

Thanks,
Yushi

title: Decrease in Quality Recently & Counterproductive Chrome-to-iOS Sync Issues
body:
PROBLEM: You must improve Chrome-to-app syncing so that we can use and reap the gold rewards for using the chrome extension on multiple devices AND this app on multiple devices. Currently, users are punished (by losing gold) when they run the extension and app simultaneously. For an app rated at #2 in productivity, this seems counterproductive.

TIMELINE: This has been an issue for over a year now (there is a Chrome extension complaint about this from Feb 2019). We paid for this app. That means you have the funds to dedicate resources to improving the Forest application. 

SOLUTION: If you’re worried about players getting gold too quickly by using multiple devices, then input an algorithm that first recognizes when multiple decides are running a session simultaneously. If a user has only one device, then they earn gold normally, with no change to the rate. The gold earned from any simultaneously-running extra devices (eg extensions or app) should be at a lesser rate.

I’ve used this app for over a year now, and it’s been good for the most part. However, the Forest app developers need to get it together. For a paid app, I expect better.

PROBLEM: App developers have ceased giving users motivators for lengthier sessions. All the new trees have just one stage for all session lengths. That’s laziness. 

SOLUTION: Make multiple stages for new trees.

Low rating to get app dev attention.

title: Best productivity booster for me
body:
Love this app! It’s very motivating to see your forest grow, work toward unlocking new trees, and be able to look back at your stats to see how much you’ve done, what you plant most, and what you spend the most time doing. I also like that you can toggle deep focus depending on the task at hand and tag your trees. I appreciate that the developers are consistently updating to fix bugs and add things like new trees.

A couple ideas for features that would be nice to see added:
-I would appreciate a feature, especially as more trees are added and the store continues to grow, that allows us to favorite trees in the store so it’s easy to find what we want to buy again when we have enough coins.
-It would be nice to be able to earn time crystals or have an option to convert from coins to time crystals. I understand that there are costs associated with developing an app and keeping it up to date, and consistent income including revenue from in-app purchases is helpful/necessary to do that for an ad-free app, but it would be nice if that feature wasn’t completely inaccessible to those of us who don’t have much money to spare after the initial app purchase but missed the trees when they first came out. (I would still expect time crystals to take more work to earn, but it would be nice if it was a possibility.)

This is one of the few productivity apps that’s actually worked for me, and I have no qualms about recommending it to anyone who’s easily distracted by their phone and looking for a productivity boost. Coming from someone who doesn’t have tons of money, I don’t regret paying for Forest at all. It’s simple but effective, customizable in the ways it needs to be, collaborative when you want to work as a team, and ad-free. Great app!

title: Updates!!! Let me arrange the trees!
body:
LOVE this app and what it does. But I think so much more could be done!

Here’s some things I think would get people to be more invested and want to use the app even more:

- be able to arrange your trees to make your garden look pretty! (This one is really needed).
- be able to change the colour of the grass / have options for different landscapes
- be able to change the background color of the app (instead of all green we can choose to make it yellow, etc.)

Just small things to help customise the experience. Really the feature I most want to happen is for us to be able to arrange the trees how we want. I want to work and then make my garden look pretty 🥺

title: eh - not worth the money

Forest is a great idea, and it works well, but all you get from your productivity w default setting is a shrub and a pine tree. So you just fill your garden with that for a while. The only thing I like better about it than flora (another productivity app) is that you can plant an actual tree without paying money, but you obviously still need a lot of coins. I prefer Flora because you just have to be productive for so long to unlock a new tree. It takes less time. The garden isn’t on a square though - which I think I’d prefer. title: Read the privacy policy!!!
body:
I was using this app for a while and decided to let my son (under 13) use it.  When I created his account, it triggered the “age mechanism“ and I was supposed to click “contact us” to obtain a code (which crashed the app.  I mentioned this bug twice and support failed to acknowledge it both times).  So I emailed support directly for the code and they said “please provide copies of two government-issued photo IDs (e.g. Social security number, driver’s license or passport) for review” and they would delete it after.  I hope I don’t need to explain why this would be a major red flag from a security perspective.  If I do, you will probably not be concerned about this review.    

Upon reading the privacy policy shared by the support team, I noticed they are collecting “geographic position; Camera permission; Storage permission; Photo Library permission;”. (and plenty more which I won’t get into).   Maybe there’s functionality in this app that I’m not using and there is actually good reason for this app to be collecting this kind of data, but, on the surface, this app seems like a pretty simple timer and I was using it for that purpose.  From reading other reviews, I believe that is what others are using it for as well.  Why on earth do you need my geographical location to set a 25 minute timer?!  

I was going to just forget about creating an account for my son and continue using the app, but, after reading the privacy policy, I decided I really have no reason to be sharing all of this data to do something that any basic timer can accomplish.  I would encourage everyone to question whether or not the risk of exposing all of this information is worth the reward of using this app.

title: Helps me Improve my Relationship with Technology
body:
Studies show that wasting time by distracting yourself with distractions from doing productive work leads to less having no motivation to complete your work for the day. 

There’s so many applications out there today on the internet to try their application for productivity using the Pomodoro technique, and implementing features to prevent getting yourself distracted all the time by sending a notification that your tree, or plant will wither if you don’t get back to work. This is an amazing feature because this shows you need to focus so you can continue working until you’ve finished or done some progress. Since progress is everything than striving for perfection which are what I’m most insecure about actually. 

However, as I realize while looking at this time management app by Freedom because they have MacOS version of Freedom.  I want a MacOS version of Forest, so I can keep Forest on my laptop too than having the chrome extension, and app from the App Store alone. If you could possibly make a Forest available for MacOS especially for Windows this can tremendously get people to improve their relationships with technology even more. 

Freedom is expensive because of their pricing options, but a Forest is better for the rational reason I got this app for $1.99 or someone wants a free app for productivity uses. 

As form of closure, this app is created for everyone who uses technology in unhealthy ways like staying up late and sleeping late at night, overworking which leads to serious health risks such as emotional exhaustion, stress, depression, and physical health issues. I would highly recommend this to anyone who are often distracted from being able to be focused.

2. Earn more coins for each tree that we unlock. It’s kind of annoying that the price of trees goes up after each purchase, but you don’t even get anything extra out of planting them besides seeing the tree in the forest (which I don’t really care about). title: Please add!!
body: I absolutely adore this app! Everything is super cute, tidy, and useful. There are a few things though that I believe could make this app better. I'd like to see more events where there are limited time trees/bushes. I remember there being an Earth Day bush and little cakes too. title: Title (Haha, review is more serious than my title)
body:
I absolutely love this app. I fee really motivated to work when I use it. Even if I’m not being productive, I’m still working on something when I use it. I love how you can cancel a tree without killing it for the first 10 seconds after planting one, but I really wish that time was longer for bigger trees. It would be pretty helpful.
      The biggest moment for me was when it came time for me to kill my first tree. I really didn’t want to kill it, but I hadn’t been working. If I hadn’t chopped it down, it would’ve opened the floodgates for me. The main difficulty for me is starting to grow my tree. If I don’t start it, I don’t have to be productive.
      I’ve had this app for under a month and I’ve already recommended it to a few people, who have all said it was really helpful.
      I definitely think this app is worth a try, and I love the little changes that come out every one in a while.

title: Forest: A cute little productivity app
body:
Yes, it is a timer app that can easily be substituted for your stock timer app on your phone or device but Forest is so much more than that. 

Every time you use the timer, you get the opportunity to plant virtual trees. The more you use the app and stay focused, the more coins you receive that you can use to unlock different kinds of species to plant into your virtual forest. 

Additionally, you can save up your coins and make an even bigger purchase (no real money need to be spent besides the initial fair price of download) and plant a real tree! 

Tags are useful to categorize how much time is dedicated to a specific task you have or will complete. Interface is simple, nice and clean. Definitely a useful app that will be in my devices for a long time.

title: Positive Inspiration is Working Bettering
body: You name it, I’ve tried it when it comes to productivity/focus aids. I was not expecting this...but somehow this tree-planting thing is strangely motivating me. I feel protective of the tree while it’s “growing”. I feel like it’s not too hard to resist my impulses until the tree is finished uling software “growing”.  With the ability to tag trees gwith various categories, my mind is exploding with the possibility of where I could be after “100 trees of #websitedesign” or a forest of #meditation or how my relationship with my kids would improve after “50 trees of #qualitytimewithkids”.   It is bite-sized so it isn’t daunting. I don’t have any guilt associated with not-planting-another-tree-right-then and it is SO fast to get started that I don’t dread it like I dread loading my scheduling software each morning.  I’m pretty safe to be productive as long as I keep planting trees and GO!  Thank you! Thank you! Thank you!

title: Helps Me Read More
body:
I learned early on that ebooks were not for me because of my tendency to get distracted by the other features of the device. Even dedicated e-readers failed to keep me focused on the page because of their tempting note-taking and highlighting features.

So I stuck with time-tested paper books. But even then the nearness of my phone made reading more challenging.

Forest helps me ignore my phone. It’s such a seemingly simple psychological trick, but it works: pick up my phone, kill a tree. It doesn’t matter that it’s not a real tree. The app successfully games my mind into behaving as if it were.

I highly recommend Forest if you, like me, feel your phone takes up too much of your attention.

title: Love my trees but is it useful?
body:
There’s definitely a productive benefit to watching a tree grow and focusing on a specific task. That’s what this app does. So, for anyone who creates content, freelances, or is looking to build a skill, this is a SIMPLE way to monitor time and focus. 

But this is not a time management app. 

It’s barely a time tracker and more of a in-app store to buy digital trees. Maybe that’s all the app wants to be. And as someone who has a deep love for tamagotchis, Im into caring for a focus Forrest with different unlock-able trees. That’s totally my bag.  

My issue is that there’s no real analytics behind how you’re spending your time. I’d love to be able to see how my time is being used. That stats they do show you are pretty shallow. 

I know the app doesn’t promise to be a habit tracker, I just see the potential of it being one. I want similar stats to programs like Mint or Instagram analytics. I also wish the animation and actual Forrest function was more dynamic. 

In all it’s an okay app but I think it could become awesome. 

P.s 
I wrote this review for a free tree.

title: Unlike All Others
body:
I personally use these types of apps to motivate me to achieve certain tasks... and many of those tasks are work-related, and thus on my phone. It helps to set a timer, with a motivation like a tree attached, for me to focus on whatever task it is. Whether it be finishing an art project, responding to messages, or clearing out my inbox. 

So many other apps don’t allow me to exit the app. This one does. A+. No glitches. Variety of trees. Fair rewards. 

I only wish I could set it for 5 minutes, or at least have the option for it to send an alert at the half-point mark.

title: Lovely App
body:
Helps me focus to study; as someone with major ADHD, it’s useful to provide motivation for short periods of time! Love the aspect of unlocking trees, just worried about whenever I unlock them all; if the app creators can make some sort of consistent and ever-expanding progression system where you always have motivations to keep gathering the coins it’d be 5 starts for me! Given that they occasionally add trees, I think they’re getting there — could definitely improve the sounds/atmosphere music offered for purchase and maybe more purchases or aspects could be added later? This is all just nitpicking though, currently I’m quite happy and highly recommend the app!

Edit: A simple addition would be a way to batch edit tags; it’s a simple fix, but would improve user interface as I create tags for classes and different aspects of projects; once a project or semester is done though, it’s tedious to individually delete — and I’m sure other people rotate through different tags as well :)

title: Makes me want to be productive!
body:
I really enjoy using this app! I recently got it and I used it on the first day I got it. 
I think the features it has is cool, too. There are different settings for the background noise and they start you out with rainfall outside a window. (You have to “earn” the others with the coins you make). Another feature I thought is helpful is the ‘deep focus’ setting that you can put the app on and if you leave the app, then your tree or bush withers and dies. It kind of forces you to put down your phone or else the thing that shows that you’ve done your work is gone.
I like being able to label the trees or bushes with the task I completed as well. My forest is growing!
The only thing I don’t like as much is how you have to wait for a long time to unlock a different type of bush or tree. It’ll probably take a week to two weeks of like, an hour in order to unlock a new tree. :/
Overall, I really enjoy this app! (Please let me have a new tree).

title: One of my go-to productivity apps
body:
It’s funny; I’ve downloaded so very many productivity and timing apps which are, admittedly, more sophisticated. However, time and again, I turn to this app to stay focused. I really enjoy it, seeing my cool trees grow.
My one complaint is how sparse the interface and “forest-view” are. . . This is the only reason I’ve taken off a star. It’s a free app; I get that. However, there are optional in-app purchases—-it seems to me that it would be worth it to the developers to put a “prettier” pic in background while growing my tree and a MUCH nicer view of my forest. I’d pay a little for this if they did it (for sure) and/or perhaps they could implement better/different in-app purchases to support such an overhaul. Anyway, would be truly my fav productivity app, and never would I stray, would they work on these aesthetics!! In the meantime, though, I’m sure I’ll continue to use this pleasing little app :)

I actually really like this little app. It’s unfortunate that there’s in game microtransactions to help unlock trees, cause the rate of gold earned is kinda poor.

An app about growing different trees through productivity is great but growing the same tree 8 times isn’t very fun... 

But the app works. I look at my phone to check the stock market and my positions, plus Snapchat way too often. So I use this to help me focus on work or whatever for a good 45 min to an hour.

Got a few different trees in my Forest now, so I’m having a good time watching it grow. Just wish it was a little faster. Almost encourages you to just let the app run all the time.

title: Different Timing Options
body:
I really like the idea of planting trees and getting coins as rewards for staying off of my phone, but choosing how many minutes to set a goal for is hard because I never know how long something is going to last.  If I set it for 30 minutes but then get an important text message from my mom, I have to give up and kill my plant.  

I would suggest having a mode that lets you just turn off your phone in the app for as long or as short of a time as you want without setting a goal.  And if we leave the app, it doesn’t kill the tree.  Just the amount of time we stay in the app without leaving it results in different colored plants and trees.  Like maybe 1-5 minutes could be a flower and maybe like 60 minutes could be a willow tree and so forth.

title: Best Productivity App Ever!
body:
I very rarely spend money on virtual things, but this app is definitely worth the $2. I have never been this productive in my life. The sheer quality of this app is amazing. Forest has a beautiful Graphical User Interface. I end up spending the most time on my phone using this app, if you don’t count Safari and Messages. Forest has a feature that displays a graph that implicates your productivity throughout the day. The feature that breaks down how much time you spend on individual activities is also quite useful and interesting. It’s genuinely a great app.

My only complaint is that you cannot rearrange the order of your tags, or the order that they show up in the pie graph. Also the Time Line tab is a bit useless. Other then that, this app is perfect.

But even though it sounds silly, having the motivation of planting a little tree truly helps. And, when I do start doing something I don’t get sidetracked on other apps because my tree would wither away. I wasn’t reading as much as I used to but with this app I’m reading quite a bit. My second point relates to my last. While the app is simple looking, looks can be deceiving and takes a bit to get used to. title: Awesome App!!
body: I have been using the Forest app for almost 2 months now and this app has been amazing!!! It has helped me be way more productive and create so many good habits!! I'm a mom with kids and it's often hard to get motivated to do housework, pay bills, etc., when the same chores stare me in the face day after day. Growing trees gives me just enough incentive to not only get things done but also I can then look back and realize at the end of the day I have actually accomplished something! Also, I have always struggled to maintain good habits such as exercise daily, eat a certain amount of fruits & veggies, get to bed on time, etc., but with this app I grow specific trees/bushes for each habit I maintain each day. I then have a record to not only help me remember to do each habit but to see how long I've maintained it. I know some reviewers mention it's "just a timer" but for me, it's the extra bit I need to motivate me especially as there is a record of my accomplishments. Also, I like that each tree/bush costs an additional 100 coins up to 1000 per tree/bush as early on that motivated me to add more things/habits I grew trees for, which then made it easier/quicker to earn enough coins for the next tree. Just be creative how you use the app!! Finally, and very importantly, I wanted to mention that I had no issues with the app until just the other day when an issue came up with trying to label the trees. I contacted the app makers through feedback under settings and they not only responded but had the bug fixed within 24 hours. For a couple dollars this app is so incredibly worth it!! Thank you!

title: I LOVE THIS!
body:

I give it 4 stars and not 5 because unless you’ve been using it for a really long time it can get kind of boring. Just because you keep planting the same tree and or bush over and over again. It takes a long time or $$$ to get something different. 

And this can make it less motivating sometimes. It would be nice to have more variety of trees and bushes available from the get go soon as you get started. 

And maybe we could add some other things too like little houses or swings and stuff and maybe people.

It would also be nice if I didn’t have to start a new forest everyday but could also have the option to just add to a world or map that stays as is. 

Other than that I love this app.

title: Not for me
body: I feel like this is a concentration tracking app more than a productivity app. You plant a tree for every task you wish to concentrate on and if you break your focus (leave the app) the tree will wither. The problem here is that I need to concentrate on work, to work I need to use my phone. This app allows you to create a white list of apps that are required for your task, however this feature is not available in IOS devices. This renders the app to be nothing more than a tea timer and a graph depicting how many times you set the tea timer. You are allowed to create your own tags, but you can’t assign a task to your session until after the session is over, this means that if you read a book 7 days in a row you plant 7 trees instead of continue to water the same tree to keep it alive. I only bought this to be a visualization of my consistency with the various aspects of my life, but the app doesn’t work this way. I don’t see why this app isn’t free with ads considering that one of its most important features does not work on iPhones.

author: Shovel boy 2000

title: Really makes a difference!
body:
I just wrote a review for SleepyTown so I thought I’d come back to update my Forest review to reflect my current opinions. This app basically got me through nursing school and boards. I recommend it 100% to anyone, whether you’re a student or just use your phone too much, and I have gifted it to college friends before to help with study focus and/or phone addiction. I used to get very distracted from my studying and needed this kind of subtle motivator to stay away from my phone for specified periods of time. I’ve heard friends recommend such free apps as tomato clock, but Forest (I always accidentally call it “Trees”) is better because you have some proof of your efforts and can gain some satisfaction from actually seeing your success and trends over time as your forest grows, and it’s gratifying. If you’re a completionist like me, it would also bring you great displeasure to have to kill a tree that you’ve invested any amount of time in, so it’s like there are stakes and consequences for cheating yourself. It’s just an extra push to go all the way and keep focusing when you feel like it would be harmless to break focus and sneak a peek at Twitter.

There are also so many beautiful tree and bush designs to encourage you to grow a gorgeous forest. If my forest is looking a little barren, I get the urge to grow some more trees, and can’t have too many of the same kind of tree, so let’s switch it up and plant some sakuras today! It’s like addictive art. I also like that, if you choose to leave your phone open while you work, at any given time you can glance at your phone and see a little motivational message to stop stalling and get back to it! You also have the option to input custom messages, but I haven’t taken advantage of that.

Another well-used feature of mine is that you can customize tags for each tree to indicate how you spent your time focusing, whether it be studying, reading, exercising, or just relaxing. You can also see those analytics in your Forest overview. Now that I am a college graduate with a big girl job, I don’t need to study as much anymore, so it is nice that I can still continue to use this app for leisure activities such as reading. I occasionally use it to get some uninterrupted sleep, as well, since I work third shift, nap a lot, and sleep at odd hours. This is okay for me since I was interested in SleepyTown but can’t get use out of it as it is not really designed for people with schedules like mine. There are even the cute Starry Tree and Moon Tree designs that I will save up for to perhaps use exclusively as sleep trees!

My request: More visual growth “stages” of a tree. After all, the longer you focus, a more interesting-looking tree is yielded. I like this feature a lot! Feel like focusing for only twenty minutes? Nah, maybe I’ll go 25 just so I can have that more interesting-looking tree instead of that boring bush. It encourages you to go to the next level and increase your ambitions if you were feeling a little lazy. That being said, I would love a couple smaller benchmarks, like maybe one at 40 minutes, as going from 20 minutes to an hour is quite a big difference when intensely studying, and a lot of the time I only want to focus for 30 or 40 minutes at a time. I rarely ever have an occasion where I need to focus for two hours at a time or where it is practical to not use my phone for two hours (unless I’m asleep, because I’m an adult, and sometimes people just need to reach me) so I never get the fanciest trees. However, one of the features they have added since I started using this app allows you to turn off Deep Focus mode so you can exit the app without killing your tree. I still have yet to try this feature as it feels a bit like breaking the spirit of the rule, but I will be experimenting with it in the future.

I hope this app continues to come out with more features, designs, and achievements as it’s been quite useful and very fun to use! Thanks for a great app.

author: Mike Masutra

title: I.LOVE.THIS.APP.
body: I've used a lot of "focus" timers before, but this is the best. You put the timer on, and depending on how long you work, you plant a tree or bush or other things you can unlock (not by purchasing, but by more deep work). After accumulating 500 coins, a REAL TREE is planted by Trees for the Future. It is moderately challenging to accumulate this number. Trees for the Future has a 90% overall score from Charity Navigator. If you leave the app to do  some internet browsing etc., you kill a tree in your own digital forest. Instead of an "exit" button, you click "give up"...which I found to be rather reinforcing. Finally, if you get texts, they come up on the screen briefly but you only officially "give up" if you exit the app and respond.

title: Great productivity app!
body:
Used this all the time to get me through studying and am still applying it in my engineering career.

Set for initial 25 mins to get yourself to focus. Keep going past your final timer for an intense work block. I have 2 different “work intensities”. The second type of work block, after the 35 mins I break for 5 mins. This is for the more boring work that doesn’t required that much focus but “needs to be done”.

I like the game aspect. Getting different trees and forcing you not to click away from the app are very helpful in making you want to do your work and keep you off your phone. 

Highly recommended

title: Amazing
body: This is probably the most useful app on my phone. I like planting little trees in my forest and being able to plant real ones too! The only thing I would change, is being able to design your own forest. The way it’s laid out is good, but it would be nice if like in SleepTown, you could customize a little forest using your existing array of trees and maybe buy little decorations, because looking at over 800 little trees at once is kinda overwhelming, and you have to go into months or weeks to actually see them. Other than that it’s literally perfect, and that’s really just a recommendation on how to make it better, but it’s perfect the way it is already!

author: snowsleepling

title: Focus for a good cause
body:
This app has been a helpful asset to building better habits in my life. Sometimes I use it as a timer/ dare to get stuff done , e.g. “I have two tasks to do, I’m going to see if I can get them done in 30 minutes.” It takes personal work to build habits and work ethic, and this app acts as a good support of that. When I first bought the app I was studying for the GRE, by the time I collected enough seeds to plant a real tree outside of the app, I was one year into graduate school and that was a pretty cool moment. (I definitely would have accumulated enough hours work before that if I used the app EVERY time I did work or studied)
I recommend this to my friends and family! We need more trees in the world, more time applying ourselves to meaningful work, (and less time on our cellphones.)

title: Perfect for students who just can’t focus!
body:
I’m a high school student, and I use this app when I have to study or take notes. For those of you who aren’t interested in reading a really long review, here’s my summary: 

This app wards off distractions and is a perfect way to keep yourself focused! 
The in-app purchases are not at all necessary (I haven’t felt even the slightest bit tempted to spend money), so you should definitely give this app a try! 

Here’s the longer explanation:

I originally heard about Forest from a friend after I told her how I was struggling to avoid getting distracted. It seemed like every time I tried to sit down and start working, a new notification popped up on my screen- whether it was a text message, an email, or a game alert- and I couldn’t stay focused.

I love this app because it helps me stay on track and get work done. With the adorable game design aside, using this app is just super gratifying! Of course, the tiny trees are cute and it’s fun to grow your own forest, but this app isn’t just aesthetically pleasing: it’s extremely functional. It allows me to focus, avoid distractions, and succeed in school. 

There’s nothing you need to buy in order to use the app, so just download it and give it a try! If it doesn’t work for you, then you can just delete it, but it might end up being super useful for you, just as it was for me!

Definitely recommend :)

title: $2 for this type of productivity is worth it
body:
Love the app. 

The Home Forest screen is good. Only thing I would change is I’d like the ability to edit my own forest/garden. Almost like a game appeal so that it’s a bit more fun. You can still do everything you’re doing (because I like seeing my productivity) and add this feature as another tab after “year” if you catch what I’m putting down

The timeline is super cute and I like the fact that I can see a detailed view because I’ve tagged my tree to what I’m doing. 

I love that I can see my friends but I hate that I can only see what they’ve been doing on that day only. Again I’d love for everyone to be able to edit their forests and for their friends to view it too. 

Achievements are cool, I haven’t unlocked any yet. It’s only my 2nd day out here 

The inventory in the store is selective and I love the choice of trees. I’d add more sound choices and I think bushes should be worth less than trees lol

It’s so cool you can actually help plant real trees with the coins you built up in the game! 

The news tab is well organized and appealing to look at. Everything about this app has a very “fun” appeal, it’s easy to use and it all ties together ☺️

title: Almost a 5 out of 5.
body:
This app is great for any student trying to reduce his/her time on their cell phone and manage how much time they spend on a certain topic or activity. 

How can it be a 5/5 for someone like me?

It would be nice to be able to export our data. 

Also since a major driving factor is competing with friends and earning medals maybe add more metals to the list as well as making competitions between friends. (Most logged hours per day or week etc.)

One last addition could be a fire crackle sound effect. 

The app does a great job in most other aspects though. As a current med student I use it a LOT to track my studies.

Update: exporting data has been added (nice)

title: Wish I knew this existed when I was in school!
body: Throughout my entire academic career, I’ve never been the type of student who could study for 6-8 hours a day. I got really anxious and resorted to checking my phone to avoid studying. I’m currently preparing for my licensing exams and desperately needed something to help me focus on studying and more importantly off my phone! I saw someone on Reddit recommend this app and figured that it’s $2, it wouldn’t hurt. To my surprise, this app has kept me accountable with studying! I follow the pomodoro method (4 25-min sessions with 5 min breaks in between). With each 25 min session, I plant a little cedar tree and my goal is to have 4 trees in 1 study session. Definitely wish I knew about this app sooner!

title: Great app, currency problem
body: I really like this app. It has a clean, easy to understand design, and the look of the trees you "plant" go well with it. I also like how the app shows your app use sessions in a virtual forest which is fun to look at. However, I feel like it takes too much currency to plant one real tree. You need 2500 in-app coins for a real tree to be planted. I tend to use the app for shorter sessions (15-30 minutes), but you get few coins per session (I get 4 coins for 10 minutes and around 20 for 30 minutes. Though this won't stop me from using the app, maybe there could be free "powerups" you can get for free, possibly by watching ads, that will allow you to receive more coins per session. Still, the app is great.

title: The best pomodoro timer
body: I have ADHD & the pomodoro technique is a god sent for me but it’s hard to find a timer or a system that will really help keep me focused. THIS is the app! I’ve used Forest in the past & then drifted and used a dozen other timers for the pomodoro technique but I always come back to forest. And now I’m here to stay! This app has everything you need to use the pomodoro technique in a way that works for you. You can set timers for 10 minutes, 20 minutes, to 60 minutes and everything in between! You can schedule your breaks and use labels and make notes on your tasks as you do them! It’s so flexible and perfect and I love the Google Chrome extension as well so I can use it on my Mac & my iPhone with no added cost! I love seeing my forest grow and the options to buy different trees and things as well! Work hard enough and Forest will plant a real tree for you! 10/10 everyone should use this app!

author: lulumewmew

title: Very Useful!
body:
Incredibly useful app, helps me stay on task! I’ve recommended it to friends, and they’ve told me they like it too. The different types of plants are not only really cute, they provide a nice incentive to keep you going. The option to plant real trees with the coins you’ve earned is also really great. It’s really easy to look back on all your different forests, and you can even connect with friends to compare, if you’re the competitive type ;^) Granted, you still need the self control to open the app and stick to it in the first place, but that’s not the app’s responsibility, haha.

Smooth design, some customizability (phrases to motivate or keep you in check while you work), reminders, and even ambience. Forest is my go-to whenever I’m studying!

title: Best productivity app!!!
body: Want to be more productive? Just set a timer and a little tree will start to sprout. Keep the app open and your tree will start to grow within the set time. If you go the whole time without using your phone the tree will grow to full size. However, if you use your phone then your tree will die. You get coins for every full grown tree you have that can be used for planting a tree in real life! What is better than being productive while helping the environment at the same time?! You can also collect different types of trees and build a colorful forest all your own.🖤👍🏼🌎

title: My productivity has grown
body:
I usually don’t buy apps, but this one is worth it! I am a very task driven person, and being able to see a concrete thing being accomplished by setting time aside to be productive helps me not give in to picking up my phone. I love the little trees you can see that you’ve built over time, and that eventually you can build a real life tree!

The only criticism I have is that I think it takes way too many coins to buy new digital trees or a real one. I understand it’s expensive to plant a new tree and they make money by people buying things to make them get more digital currency, but it seems hard to set your goals to plant a real life when the goals seem unattainable. 

Regardless, this is definitely the best productivity app I’ve used! Worth the $2!

title: Keeps You Accountable
body:
This app simultaneously irritates me and doesn’t, because it does its job so well! You set the timer as to how long you want to focus on something and a tree starts growing. If you close the app your tree will die. The only downside to it is now I can’t use my phone to procrastinate work. Oh, and, you can’t really change your music while growing a tree because leaving the app kills it. I like the in app sounds, too, they’re peaceful. You can mute them if you like, but I find myself listening to the bird chirping anyways.

Long story short, I love it because it keeps me from getting distracted! 
(And you grow a cute tree)

title: Needs more improvement. Too similar to Flora.
body: I like the way this app works. However, I found the function of this app very similar to the app flora (which is free). I think that you need to add more functions and features to make this app worth the money like break time and make the app more different from flora. Sometimes, when I’m doing homework and I need a break, I can’t stop the timer and the break time is counted as my studying time. I would love a break time function! I also think you should make this app more like a game. I love games and it’s the reason why I downloaded this app. You should add levels, character shops, more rewards, maybe competition to motivate people, motivation quotes, more items in shops, studying tips, functions that help concentration like to do lists, and make sure the features or functions that are new are not distractions and helpful to make the app fun and motivating. title: Love this app, but here’s my only complaint
body:
So experience wise, i think it’s great. The only thing i would change is how the tiles form with more trees you plant. Because the tiles keep growing at a rate higher than the amount of trees you plant, your forest is always looking emptier than it should, leaving you feeling unsatisfied.

You could make the argument that the empty tiles incentivizes the users to plant more trees, but I’d wager that users will most likely use the app longer if they’re able to consistently feel that their forest is jampacked with trees, and not sparsely potted. If you’re a designer for the app reading this, hope this influences your decision to update the algorithm for the tiles. :)

title: Review as requested by app.
body:
TOP LINE: Meh, so far. It looks pretty. It’s stable. It’s cheap. Poor user support and tutorial. Limited use compared to other “Pomodoro” type apps.  Buy if curious. Skip if you’re happy with your system.

PRO: the app (1) looks pretty and (2) is stable within the current version of iOS (12.x.x). (3) Reasonable one-time price for most features.

CON: (1) very weak tutorial. Much seems to be figure out as you go. (2) Poor user accessible support. Ex: App Settings -> FAQs -> blank page with spinning circle. Waited for a full minute. Still spinning. (3.) Arbitrary request for review instead of, “How are we doing?”  I’ve seen other apps, in their tutorial, mention they’d really appreciate a review but they don’t interrupt your workflow.

NEUTRAL: I wish Apple didn’t restrict putting specific apps on the Whitelist. That would have been a great boon if possible. That said, I’d imagine the developers are more frustrated about that than I am.

So that’s my review as requested.

Hopefully, I’ll learn how to get more out of this app and will update my review at that point.

title: Truly and brilliantly unique, Forest is a must
body:
It brings together two vastly different ideas that are perfectly suited to empower the other.

Forest helps you spend less time on your phone unlike anything out there. Everyone suffers from a varying degree of cell phone addiction and we all know we need to cut back. 

With Forest, it’s simple. You plant a virtual tree on your phone for a set amount of time, if you use your phone before the time is up, you kill your tree 😳. Or you can wait another 15 minutes and the tree thrives. Still, so what? The trees aren’t real... right? Wrong! The less time you waste on your phone, the more your trees grow, the more REAL TREES ARE PLANTED. 

That’s right, save up enough of your in game currency and Forest’s partner organization Trees for the Future will plant a real living tree. So we all spend less time on social media, YouTube, and Candy Crush... more with the people in our lives who matter, and hundreds of thousands of trees are being planted as a result.

What are you waiting for?

title: Excellent way to gamify productivity
body:
The reward system in Forest really helps to motivate me to remain focused during work sessions. 

I’m giving only four stars because I dislike most of the tree illustrations—apart from the default tree and bush, all other tree illustrations appear childish and have toys or other debris hanging from the branches like Christmas decorations.  

I would love to see a less light-hearted approach taken with some of the unlockable tree types that caters more to mature audiences or those who enjoy realism in gaming.

As a home gardener, I would also enjoy reading interesting facts about the chosen specie of tree if they to appear on the “success” popup that appears if a tree is successfully grown.

title: Great way to focus and get stuff done
body:
Its a great app if you need to get anything done, work, sleep, or just can’t put down your phone, it works very well. Seeing the amount of trees you’ve grown over the month is very satisfying and actually quite difficult/heartbreaking to kill trees, I haven’t killed one yet. A few notes though: there isn’t a way to end a timer if you got all your work done, meaning even if you have everything done, you still have to either wait for the tree, or kill the tree. I wish there was a good way to get the work done, maybe change it for a different tree, but something so you don’t have to kill the tree but don’t have to wait 20 minutes.

A few quick things about the app;

Parents:
This is not a good way to make your child get work done as they still have the choice to get out and will get out if this is against their will. I am not a condoner of things like OurPact, there are better ways to control your child and let them get their work done

Students/anyone else:
This app is a great way to stay encouraged and not have the distraction of your own phone, I count computer games as killing the tree though, so you set your own rules and get down to getting your work done!

I wish you the best of luck!

title: So helpful!
body:
This app has provided me all the incentive I need to stay focused. In this world of nearly constant connectivity, having the app encourage me to ignore my phone has also helped me put aside emails, other side tasks, and in-office distractions in favor of writing. I first used this app during a writing workshop and got so much done that I decided to incorporate it into my daily writing practice, and I have not been disappointed with the results! Thank you! 

I do wish that the app played a sound when a tree has grown. I also wish that there was a way to allow the app to turn off notifications, because if I leave my phone screen up so I can see when the tree is done, I also see my text messages, emails, etc. come in. I don’t open them, but I still wish I could have screen silence while working on a tree. I’ll investigate playing around with my settings. Maybe there’s already a way to accomplish this!

title: Dramatic increase in productivity!
body: In my case, the phone has always been a huge distraction of mine. Forest, utilizes evidence based methods of productivity, known as the Pomodoro technique, that many successful people have utilized to accomplish their goals. This technique provides a strict study schedule to follow (25 work, 5 min break, repeat), which not only helps you stay focused for greater lengths of time but the app itself also applies its own twist on this technique by one, making it harder to get distracted by using your phone, and two: allowing you to see the fruits of your labor in an aesthetic and rewarding manner. The one dollar it costs is more than worth it. P. S. I’m also studying for the MCAT.

title: Effective but can be improved
body:
I’ve been using the app for a few years and love how it motivates me to stay on task. That said, I think it’s time for this app to do far more to really facilitate better focus.

The Pomodoro Technique is effective for a lot of people because you can move between productive time and small breaks. The way this app works, however, is that if you want to plant a tree to its full size you need to focus for two hours straight otherwise it dies or you get a small, not as cute looking tree stub. Frankly, I don’t know anyone nowadays who does that. That’s 1/12 of the whole day already. As a student, I need breaks like most people do. Other productivity apps have this option and I think the devs should consider incorporating a Pomodoro Technique option when you decide to focus for longer than 25 minutes.

This is frustrating because I slaved away to earn 1000 coins on buying a cute tree that I can’t focus long enough for. To contextualize, you get 5-6 coins per 20min study and the number of coins earned increases the longer you study in one session. You can imagine how many hours I spent with this app to buy a few trees. These days though, the shrubs are clearly more valuable because the focus-time for those is 20 min at most. 

Please consider incorporating a Pomodoro Technique mechanic. 

Just to note, I suggested this in-app but received no response which is why I’m finally posting a review.

title: Forest is my new favorite app
body: I’ll be honest: I’m a student, and I spend WAY TOO MUCH time on my phone. It is a major distraction and I can feel myself getting sucked in but was having trouble ever convincing myself to just put it down and get stuff done. I never buy apps (I only go for the free versions of everything) — I literally just paid actual money for my first app ever earlier this year, after owning a smart phone for the past 6 years. This app is well worth the $2. It helps motivate me to stay off my phone when I’m practicing (music student) or trying to get work done. My boyfriend also has the app and we’ve made rooms to help us both focus simultaneously a few times but I’m hoping to get more friends to buy it so I can do this more. It is the perfect combination of motivating and making you feel disappointed in yourself if you slip up 😂 Seriously, it’s so satisfying to watch your forest grow and it’s very easy to use. You can also create new “tags” for why the trees were planted, which I love (I made one specific for practicing which is also a good way to help me keep track of how much practice I do). I had tried setting time limits for screen time/social media through iPhone settings but I’ve already started ignoring that....but Forest is so much more convincing and I just can’t let my sweet little trees die lol. Overall I love love this app and wish I’d heard of it sooner! It’s a relief to have something really hold me accountable for my screen time!

title: Good enough but could be much better
body:
Effective for keeping your phone away from distractions. With the chrome extension, this app is good for fighting distractions. 
Good for tracking “focus time”. However, the tree reward is not really much of a reward. Not sure if it’s worth the 1.99 price tag especially because the app can’t sync automatically with the chrome extension so if you’re using both at the same time it doubles the amount of time recorded scaling back the feature that made it useful in the first place.

+5 stars for effectiveness — gives you a goal for focusing and tracking/visualizing focus times
-1 Star for not syncing 
-2 Stars for 1.99 price tag and stingy coin rewards: need 500 to buy a tree but focusing for 30-40 minute intervals (optimal focus times) got you only 10-20 coins encouraging users to do in app purchases. For a paid app, this seems greedy.

title: Got it for the cute interface, stayed for the productivity increase
body:
I’ve only been using this app for around a week, but it’s already cut down on the amount of time I absent-mindedly use my phone.  Initially I got it mostly for how cute the little forests look, I’ll admit, and for the fact that earning enough in-game currency lets you plant a REAL tree!  Now, it even helps me keep my phone away when going to bed (a big hurdle for me), since I set it to the longest break setting (2 hr) as I’m laying down.

Obviously, how people use their phone-free time will vary.  For me, it’s allowed (forced?) me to eat my meals uninterrupted by scrolling, and I’ve begun creating art more frequently again (as I would always get stuck in the loop of “looking for inspiration” on my phone and then never actually getting to the art).

Honestly this is the best app I’ve ever paid money for (and one of the very few I shelled out cash for period), and it’s been completely worth it.  If you spend upwards of 4 hours a day on your phone (like I was doing), I highly recommend taking this app into consideration!
