title: Good app, helps me focus
body: This is a good app. I have been using it since 2015 and I am pretty satisfied with it. The new tree/bush species are beautiful and having different species really does motivate me to keep planting my garden and to earn more coins so I can unlock a new species. I have huge issues with wasting time on my phone and time management due to executive function issues and mental illness and this app has helped me a lot as a college student. The app can’t force you to do your work, but it CAN force you to take a break from your phone, and that ten minute break can be really, really useful when you are stuck. I also love that you can input custom tags to  track and categorize different categories of planting time (sleeping, class time, homework time, etc) and that you can see your progress on the graph. The options to keep the screen on, track exceeded time, and ding or send a notification when the tree is done are also really helpful for me. My only suggestion would be to show us a better preview of what a tree will look like when planted for a shorter time before we pay coins to unlock it. For example, the preview image for the apple tree shows a big apple tree with apples and a picnic basket, but once you buy the tree you realize that you can’t get it to look that pretty unless you are able to plant it for a longer time, like 40 minutes+. If you are only planting trees for less time, like 30 minutes or less, then a lot of the trees look kind of the same and they are not as colorful or as big as pictured in the store, because they don’t “grow” to look like the picture. Overall I love your app and would absolutely recommend it to anyone who is struggling to break away from their phone. Thank you, Forest app developers! ❤️🌳

title: Cheating and no breaks
body:
I like the app and use it often but I find there are two major problems: first, the leaderboards and earning points for doing so. I use this app honestly when I’m really focusing, but people who choose to can log onto Facebook or whatever on a computer or another phone and rack up points, climbing the leaderboards for nothing.
Secondly, I wish there was a “break” option during focus sessions. I find I do well with intervals of focus and break like 20/5 minutes or 30/10. The app rewards long uninterrupted focus times and sometimes that’s just more tiring than efficient. Would be nice to get the same amount of points for a two hour max session with a couple 5-10 minute breaks in between.

title: Fun Incentive to Stay Focused
body: LOVE this app! I have ADD and tend to procrastinate the important things I need to do at work and social media is the perfect tool to do so- however this app has been super helpful with staying off of it. The premise of it may sound cheesy or like it wouldn’t be that motivating but it’s become a game for me to see how long I can stay off of it. And the fact that you get to plant real trees once you’ve earned enough coins to do so is 1. personally a good enough reason to pay for the app and 2. an even bigger motivation to stay off my phone while it’s turned on or else it’ll “kill the tree” (just on the app) that I’m in the middle of “growing.” Definitely recommend to anyone who needs help with self-discipline!

title: Keeps me from falling in YouTube hole
body: I recently bought this app and am not disappointed. I grow trees at work, which helps keep me from using my phone to procrastinate. I also LOVE the rain sounds, because I work in an open concept space. Even though they pump white noise through speakers on our floor, I can still hear people nearby clacking away on their keyboards with their fake nails, coughing incessantly, or complaining. With this app, I focus on my work, and listen to soothing rain sounds to drown out the rest of that noise. At home, I plant my forest instead of falling into a YouTube vid watching, hours long session spiral. It stops me from wasting hours and keeps me thinking about what I really want to do. I do waste a little time picking which tree I’m going to plant next though...love this app. My only gripe is I haven’t quite figured out how to use the tag feature. Doesn’t really matter too much to me though. Suggestions to add in might be more achievements or “easter egg” type items for staying focused for a certain amount of time or for planting a certain tree so many time etc. Items could be treasure chests , bonus point elixirs, or just an extra fun item to put in the forest for free (like an animal or statue or something. Just some thoughts...Anyway, I highly recommend!

title: Have used app for 2.5 years, and I love it
body: I’ve been using the Forest app for the past 2.5 years, and it’s survived the chopping block this whole time. Being a college student with ADHD, this app has helped me so much because there are times where I can get distracted by Instagram or FB for hours. I love the concept of planting trees and being able to see how much you’ve stayed focus for a day, week, month, or year. I also love that you have the ability to help plant a real tree. That being said, I do wish I was able to see the timer on my lock screen, so that by just turning on my phone I would be able to see the time left. I usually leave my phone on silent or do not disturb while studying, so I don’t get the notification that my tree has been planted.

title: Cute!
body: It’s $2, and I’m usually not a person to pay for an app. After all, I like to not be distracted by my phone. Why would I pay to be distracted? I’d recommend it for Android users and for those who already know a bunch of people who use it. I have an IPhone and I can’t waitlist any apps, which is a bummer because I contact group members using my phone when working on lab reports. Still, I like the biodiversity I achieve when joining other people’s study sessions. I have trouble getting motivated to get out of bed sometimes, but because I want the cutest forest of the day, I find a reason to stay focus, like getting ready, and it feels like a major accomplishment. My friends have collectively planted 5 real trees as of now, so I look forward to adding to that someday.

title: Helps you stay on task!
body: This app is good for those who unconsciously move their hand to their phone and then get distracted for 4 hours! In other words, someone like me... If you have a heart and do not have the audacity to kill a pure, growing, virtual plant, then give this app a shot. It helps me stay away from mindlessly going on social media just to check “something”. I get sidetracked very easily and I’ve been wanting to improve that habit because I end up being less productive. Unlocking my phone and witnessing my little seedling growing seems so pure that I allow it to grow. (Most of the time. There had been some incidents.) If you’re like me and are easily distracted and you lose focus often on what needs to be done, by all means try this app out if you lack the mental stability of ignoring your apps.

title: Hands down one of the BEST productivity app!!! OMG!!
body: I friggin LOVVVVVEEEEEE THIS APP!!! I used to use a regular pomodoro app that just automatically do 25 mins with 5 mins breaks. I’ve used it for a long time until I got introduced to the forest app. I didn’t even bother with the free version, I just bought this app and it was the best $0.99 I’ve ever spent!! It’s literally the best way to gamify your life in a smart way! I absolutely love this new updates with the new graphs and pie charts, like I can’t stop gushing about this app. I’ve been consistently using this app for a good month now and it is going to be in my collection for life. My only tiny itty bitty wish is that I could have the option to use the 12 hour timeline clock rather than the 24 hour military time clock. Other than that, this app is perfection and I 10/10 recommend this to everyone. If I could give this app a 100/100 stars I would!!! Keep it up Forest App crew!!

title: Love This App, Would Recommend
body: Well-balanced mix of gamification, environmentalism, and social aspects. The art is also really wonderful and cute! Makes my pomodoros feel effortless, and gives me motivation to do work with friends. I like that it takes a significant amount of time for me to gain enough coins to get more trees, it makes the purchases feel important. I also like getting friends trees when they host the session. I do think the social connection could use a little work — I have never gotten a pop up when my friends send group requests, and have always needed to fill out the code, which really increases the effort as you need to connect for each tree. Regardless, I think the positives of this app highly outweigh that shortcoming, and would recommend this app to anyone wanting to try and keep a healthy work-break balance.

author: Hdaks w

title: Satisfying and Full of Potential
body:
I don’t write nearly as many reviews for apps that I enjoy as I should. I had to for this one. While I’d enjoy a few added things, they’d be additional sources of happiness that are not necessary to love this app. I’d enjoy different themes (seasonal would be apropos as well as dark for those of us with migraines and eye strain) and an ability to temporarily increase our yield of points (I’d be good with watching a few ads in exchange for that). Maybe the option to have a quote when you finish a tree would be a cool way to end your session; you could even choose to get an expanded quote pack on success or wisdom or happiness or pop culture for coins or as an in-app purchase. 

Having a place to look over quotes you enjoyed would be nice. Being able to post a picture to show what you did while you were focused would be cool. While I often write on my computer while I have the timer up, sometimes I spend the time with my family or I do some art. It would be cool to show the fruits of my labors instead of just having a tag in those instances. If having a “photo view” of your forest would be an added purchase option, that would be fine too.

I’d like a few more sounds added, but I have faith they’ll be added to like the trees are. I really like that the devs are adding new trees and bushes, and it makes me kind of push myself to keep going. But it’s also very frustrating; I feel the price increase per new plant or sound purchase is too steep. I’m not a huge fan of that. I mean, at some point it’ll cost more to get access to a kind of tree or bush or sound than it would to actually plant a tree IRL. That’s... super frustrating.

I love the idea of rooms. I think it would be cool if there was some sort of boost, or reward for working together. It can be a bit of a hassle to arrange it but if you could plant a certain kind of tree (and after doing
it as a group a certain amount of times, you can plant that kind solo), or if you get more coins per minute, or maybe if you get a wildcard tree, that would be great. 

I also like the idea of rewarding app fidelity. That maybe if you plant every day for a week, you get to plant one tree of any variety regardless of it it’s unlocked or not. Or you get half an hour of listening to a sound you haven’t fully unlocked. Or if you check in every day to “water” your investment with your forest, you get some kind of reward. I am motivated to a ridiculous extent by achievements and streaks (I have a 550 day Duolingo streak as I type) and the better the reward system is implemented, the more likely I am to feel invested in the app and loyal, to an extent. Once I kind of work through the existing rewards and I’ve already reached the cap of having five trees planted IRL I may well get bored with this app and move on to something else, despite really enjoying the layout and idea, because if progress is so slow it’s barely noticeable at all, and I’ve already achieved most of what I can, I’m going to see if other apps have popped up that can offer me something more engaging that has new and more extensive rewards and achievements to go through, to challenge myself.

The more this also functions also as a memory holder (with photos and memories and quotes) the less likely I am to eventually drop it. If it needs to stay very streamlined as it is, then broader achievements or a less steep curve in terms of adding trees to the collection would be great.

I really like being able to add tags with the upgrade; I can look back and see if I was reading or writing and what genre it was, see at a glance what kind of month I was having. 

A note would be that I wish the reward system worked a bit differently. You’re not incentivized to spend more time being productive. While I love that it doesn’t make it not worth your time to use the app for short periods of time, it also would be better for me if I had three sets of 20min sessions instead of one 60min one. I think having a few idealized time slots around half an hour apart is a good idea, and it would be a nice little perk for the nerds in the room who took the time to do the math and figure out just how many coins you’re getting per minute after each 5min increase is accounted for. But it feels sort of random and haphazardly done right now, no rhyme or reason to it, there’s no pattern to it. Does the app want me to log more time? Which, is what most apps what? If so, then why don’t I get more coins per minute if I commit to a long session instead of a shorter one? It doesn’t really make sense to me, and I’m sure there are other people who were trying to work out how to maximize their system that became puzzled and perplexed about it.

I like that there is added detail the longer you stick with the app. You have a smaller and less detailed tree at half an hour than you do at an hour, etc. I think that is really snazzy.

I feel like just... a little more customization would be cool. Being able to pick having leaves instead of grass under your trees, or pine needles, or moss, or even have like a cotton candy dreamscape backdrop or theme for it if you want. There may be people who would love the first week of April to have a cotton candy grass theme and only plant cotton candy trees that week. Or if you’re happy it’s officially autumn you can do an autumn leaf theme.

Having a little bird or squirrel or something be able to perch in a branch now and then would be cool. Like, if you plant 50 bushes in a week, you get a lady bug, you can choose to place it somewhere on a bush in the forest for the week.

Also something I’d like would be a remembrance tree. My Mom has cancer so when she has bad days, I plant her favorite kind of tree, because I’m thinking of her. But, if she died, I’d want to memorialize that in some way other than just tagging one tree. Having a Memory Tree would be nice.

I really like the app. I hope it grows. It has a lot of potential; I’m excited to see where it goes. There’s a lot that could be done here.

title: love it
body:
honestly, i love this app so much. it helps me stay focused and forces me to stay off my phone. With my struggles with ADHD, I just need some motivation and discipline to help me get started and this is the perfect program to help me through that. there are other apps very similar to this one that are free, but I would recommend spending the .99 to buy this one because the money actually goes to contributing to a good cause - by planting actual trees. 

there are only a few parts that make it difficult at times. sometimes i need to do a homework assignment but i need a photo of a sheet of paper or take notes from my browser online, and i cannot do that while running the app without killing the tree. it would be really helpful to have a white list to allow certain apps or websites. or maybe you could just implement a feature to allow for an upload of a picture or screenshot so you can use it as a reference while using the app. While there is the option to work with the phone, it is easy to become distracted if I am able to access everything.

Another possible feature that would be helpful / beneficial could be to set some sort of goal for the day/ week? A lot of times I forget about the app and struggle until I force myself to go back to it; I tend to use it in bursts (many hours in the span of 3 days but nothing for two weeks). If it could send a notification like “hey, do you want to do xyz so that you can meet your goal?” and then you can get extra coins or something if you meet the goal. 

However, overall this app is wonderful, works great, and I would definitely recommend it to anyone that needs to focus and is motivated by collecting cute things haha

title: A modest, but wonderful app.
body:
I’ve owned this app for about a year and a half. I’m trying to write a book and Forest has helped me immensely in this regard. Previous attempts have always ended fizzled out, either because of lack of time or inspiration. Since February 2018 I’ve been using Forest as a means to take time and focus on my writing. I use the Pomodoro technique of 25 minutes of pure focused work and use Forest to track this.

I now have over 90,000 words and while I still have a ways to go, for the first time ever I feel that I am reaching my potential as a writer. I don’t normally write app reviews, but Forest has been such a great part of my writing process that I felt it deserved five minutes of my time to praise it.

title: Put your phone down!
body: I love this app. It’s super fun to pick a tree each time so it doesn’t feel like I’m being deprived of phone time or getting tsk-tsked about my usage. It’s very customizable and flexible so I can tweak everything to help me get the most out of it. The timer lets you set your time anywhere from 15-120 minutes, which is a very useful range. Ambient sound is an available option during each planting and you can even change sounds mid-tree without harming your growth. For each successful tree you receive coins to buy new trees, contribute to a real-life forest, or unlock new ambient sounds. I use the app for myself, to keep me off my phone during work time, dinner, or family time, but my kids also like to use it. I set a timer and turn on ambient sound for my little one’s nap time or we set a timer so they grow a tree during chore time. It’s been incredibly useful to my whole family.

title: Guilt Motivation Works!
body:
I absolutely love this app. In fact, it’s so effective that it almost has the opposite effect – it’s addicting! That being said, it is extremely effective In that it does really make you think whenever you mindlessly pick up your phone of what you’re doing. The immediate guilt trip of having a tree that might die if you don’t immediately stop using your phone is perfect and usually all the reminder you need.

What I will say is that you can circumvent the app if you’re really dedicated. It lets you navigate away for a few seconds at a time, so if you just want to send a quick text response, you can usually get in a word or two and send it and then get back to the app before the tree dies. However, the alternative is to kill the tree every time you accidentally open your phone and navigate away from the app, Which is a little much, so I think it’s just up to us to be responsible adults and use the app the way it’s meant to be used.

The positive reinforcement of being able to buy new trees and shrubs, and see all the variety the more time you spend focused, is Probably the thing that gives it return value. If you were just punished for not focusing, it would be easy to stop using the app. However, the creative and fun new options keep me interested, and I even find myself starting themes for the week or the month with different types of trees!

The only wish I have for this app is that you were able to grow trees in specific places on your grid. It would be so cool to be able to start a row or pattern of different types of trees or shrubs, and honestly give even more motivation to spend more time focused. However, that may just be me being a little bit OCD. It’s still cool when they pop up in random places.

Certainly worth $2 to gain hours of motivated focus!

title: As Effective as You Are Honest With It
body:
Forest has been a good tool for preserving both my productivity and phone battery. The pie chart it provides (after you tag each session with a category) also helps break down where your time on Forest is going. 

As a more competitive person, having a ranking system between my friends and I is helpful. Having more trees and bushes is something I enjoy looking forward to; the last update was a fun experience. While I understand the idea of an increasing 100 coin cost with each tree bought, I found myself taking a mental L after prices started going beyond 1000.

Otherwise animated trees. That’d be amazing, and I wouldn’t mind earning a ton for coins for those.

Something that might be fun to see in the future are personal challenges. I enjoy the achievements and their rewards offered by the app (i.e. X consecutive days rewards and X many days’ worth of focus time for coins), and it would be nice to see more of them. Reward variety in the form of exclusive trees/bushes or planting actual trees is also something that’d be cool to have.

TL;DR: effective app. More trees (animated trees? ✨) and bushes to purchase/earn and more achievements with rewards would be cool.

title: Excellent app with one minor exception
body: Forest is an excellent Pomodoro-style app for blocking out time for tasks. The only thing I would change about the app is to allow for time blocks below 10 minutes. Sometimes I have tasks I do not even want to spend 10 minutes on, and I think a five minute or even a one minute timer would motivate me to get those tiny tasks done. These are the kinds of tasks that do not benefit from overlearning, so setting a ten minute time on them doesn’t make sense. You might ask why set a timer for them anyway—but sometimes it’s about tricking the mind to just get started. That’s what this app is great for: tricking your mind to get stuff done.

title: My homework is done before I eat dinner now.
body:
I love this app so much and use it to study and do my homework every night. I had a huge problem of going on my phone or watching YouTube while I was doing homework and that was always super distracting. I used to pull all-nighters all the time because I was such a big procrastinator. I love the way you can also plant real trees if you save up enough coins. It almost feels like a competitive game to me and my friends and I have a bet going for who can grow the most trees. So far, I’m winning. Coming from someone who was a big procrastinator and who often went to school with no sleep in her system, I highly recommend. This app is the best. I have to say. One small problem is that sometimes the app can be hard to navigate but you get used to it. 

Please note- I’m in all AP classes and get a bunch of homework. So having my homework mostly done before dinner at 6:00, (I get home at 2:00) is a big accomplishment.
author: Aaaaaahhhhhhhhhh!!!!!!!!!!

title: Great app!
body:
I have ADHD and this app has been incredibly helpful! It’s greatly improved my ability to stay on task and off my phone.

My biggest problem when working is I don’t realize I’ve gotten distracted. Before it was easy to just pick up my phone and spend hours not doing anything.

Now when I pick up my phone I see the forest app I realize I’m distracted. It’s an amazing mental stop and is usually enough to get me to go back on task. 

If not the little trees are cute and I know it sounds silly but I don’t want to kill a tree to check reddit. If you do kill a tree it also will put a dead tree in your forest. 

You can also unlock new trees with coins. You get coins by putting more trees in your forest so it’s kinda a motivational thing to focus more to unlock more trees. (You can also unlock sounds to listen to while you focus.) 

The app is a great tool for anyone who gets mindlessly distracted and doesn’t realize. It’ll keep your phone from being a distraction point at a minimum. (It’s not magic unfortunately and won’t stop other distractions).

If you’re the kinda person who deliberately procrastinates or realizes that you are distracted it may or may not help. It depends how much you can bring yourself to care about the app. 

It’s helped me an incredible amount and I am thankful for the app.

title: Where did my coins go???
body:
I was 1 coin away from having 900 coins, enough to buy a new tree and I was very excited. I planted a bush for 10 minutes and now I’m at 867?? You can only imagine my disappointment. Is it charging me to plant trees? If so, then it’s a dumb feature and just makes me want to stop using the app. If it was a bug on your part, then I want my coins back 😡 I worked hard for those. They’re not easy to accumulate. 

But overall, I’m giving this app 4 stars (5 if I get my coins back). When I was referred by a friend I thought it was silly but it’s literally the only thing that keeps from using my phone when studying. You’d think planting fake trees (you can also save up to plant a real tree) wouldn’t be motivation enough but it is!!! If you convince your friends to buy this app, you can create a room and study together and hold each other accountable! My friends and I compare the trees we have and are always eager to expand our forest. Great app! Just give me coins back 😫. 

A suggestion: bushes SHOULD NOT cost the same as trees. That’s ridiculous, especially when the price increases with every buy.

title: So much potential!
body:

I think it can improve in some things though- I’d love to be able to sync my contacts from Gmail/Hotmail to get more friends. I’ve been trying to recommend this to my friends and I just end up taking a screenshot of my forest to explain the app. It’d be nice to have a way to share the app with my friends through the app. Where I press a link that will allow me to send a brief idea of the app. 

I would love to be able to send some type of nudge to friends when I’m looking for people to start a room with. 

It would be great if it did more analysis on my hours of focused time. For example, that it can tell me if I tend to stay more focused at a certain time of the day or how many hours total I’ve focused to a specific tag this week/month/year. 

I absolutely love it and I’m looking forward to seeing this app reach its full potential!

title: so good for focusing!
body:
let me just say that this is hands down the BEST app i have ever paid money for.  at first when i bought this app, last year, i wasn’t really in the right mindset to make the most of it.  i didn’t really use it and felt no motivation to use it.  but this year i decided i wanted to be more productive, and not waste time on my phone.  when the new school year started, i had a system: get home from school. eat a snack.  browse social media for 10-15 minutes MAX.  then i’d go to my room and open the forest app, and set it to 25 minutes.  for 25 minutes i do nothing but the task i have in front of me, no distractions, ringer off.  when the 25 minutes are up, i set the break timer to 2-5 minutes, depending on how hard the task was.  during this time i get some water or a snack, stretch, do a mini workout (pull-ups are a quick one), answer any texts, or go outside for some fresh air.  then when my timer is up, i get back to work and do another 25 minutes.  and i keep doing this until i’m about halfway through with all of my work for the day, and i take a 10 minute break to really process the information i took notes on or just take a break.  then i get back to work and repeat the 25 minutes of work, 2-5 minute break cycle.  this system has COMPLETELY changed how i get my work done.  instead of procrastinating and doing it all last minute, or doing 2-3 hours with no breaks, i do a decent amount of work with enough break time in between that i don’t get too exhausted.  one thing if you try to use this method or something similar—while you’re on the break in between work sessions, i recommend NOT going through social media.  answering texts is fine, but i find that for me if i look at social media it’s very hard to go back to work, and i ignore the “get back to work!” notifications.  even if you don’t use this exact system, or something similar, i recommend taking a few breaks because it really does help you understand what you are actually doing.  my grades have gone up a lot after i started using the app for homework, and i have much more free time to do fun things once i’m done with all my homework.  i highly recommend this app to anyone who has work or homework they have to do, and anyone who has a phone and struggles with putting it down and not getting distracted.  i’m sorry this is such a long review, it’s the only review i’ve ever written for anything.  i just felt that people should know how amazing this app is and how it can completely change your life!  also as a bonus when you complete your 25 minutes or whatever time you set, you get credits which you can use to get new types of trees, or if you want you can use them to plant real trees in real life!  

in conclusion. BUY THIS APP :)

title: Honestly a game-changer
body:
Don’t get me wrong, my phone is a useful tool, and I wouldn’t necessarily say I’m addicted to it. However, it’s also a super easy way to waste time you don’t even realize you could be using on other things. I use Forest mostly in small increments, and it keeps me from picking up my phone whenever I have a few free minutes and get bored. Since I don’t actually need or want to be on my phone, the small motivation of growing little bushes and trees is enough for me to direct my attention elsewhere- and it turns out that those few free minutes throughout the day can translate into a lot of extra productivity!

Otherwise: initial download price might seem a bit high, but considering that they plant real trees if you make enough coins to buy the option, the $2 is warranted. Coin prices in the app are average, but payment per tree during the week is okay and you can make enough yourself with a little effort (I personally think you should make a little more per tree than they offer, but it’s not a bad amount either). The interface is simple and intuitive, the art is charming and stylistically uniform, and my favorite part- the white noise options- are incredibly helpful for studying and neither overly expensive or so complicated that they become distracting.

All in all, great app that I use frequently. $2 has never bought me so much extra productivity.

One day, during my procrastination addiction, I was looking though some apps and I saw it: Forest-Stay Focused. I immediately felt drawn. “I’ll just keep procrastinating and sleazing it up while I check out this app,” I thought. Unbeknownst to my Sleazy Habits, this app would soon become the death them. I use it all the time and have gone from not studying or doing homework at all, to working on homework and studying for over 3 solid hours a day (and growing! As is my forest!). This app is awesome, and I can actually feel my Super Saiyan Sleaze Power leave me. Best $2 I ever spent. 

If you think about it, I’m only giving up like, a snickers bar and like, one or two 4-packs of Wrigley’s gum. Also, I can’t wait to unlock mushrooms and start sleazing it up with them.

title: Incredible and Effective
body:

This app is different. The fact that it’s like a game where you can watch beautiful things grow and even make a real difference by planting a tree in the real forest is so motivating. Now when I start scrolling I plant a two hour tree so I can read, practice music, do yoga, or a multitude of other productive things. 

Thank you so much for creating a wonderful app! Looking forward to more trees and more updates in the future :) 

One suggestion. I think it’d be really cool if you could have a custom forest where you could pick and choose trees and bushes to decorate your own plot of land!

title: Not ideal for Pomodoros but cute
body: I purchased this app hoping that this could help improve focus on my tasks and support use of the Pomodoro method.  The idea of having a visual outcome of a virtual forest to show a productive day sounded great.  The issue is, while you can certainly set the timer to 25 min blocks of time, this means you can only get the less ornamental (just above the base-model/bush) version of trees since the fanciest versions require setting the timer to longer stretches of time.  Over time, this has led to me having to use a second timer to break down a 2 hour block into the 25 min/5 min Pomodoro segments, which ultimately shows the app’s limited usefulness as a fun, standalone task timer. As a result, my use of the app has gradually fallen off (still trying though). One thing that revived my interest was the  developers putting holiday themes for the trees/bushes in December.  It was a nice touch.

body:

Even though the app is on my phone (so my computer is still available), I have no desire to “cheat”. What is the point in a forest full of trees you didn’t earn?

One overall suggestion I will make is that the sky is the limit with an app like this. How about a building? A town? A farm? An amusement park? There is definitely a lot of potential here if a talented group of programers want to expand on this whole idea.

For immediate improvements I would like more it the shop. I have a feeling that will keep coming though.

title: Incredible! I’m amazed.
body:
In the first stage, you ignore the app. You continue procrastinating and slacking, the app serving only as a reminder of your ideal, more focused self.

In the second stage, you open the app. You fail numerous times and your efforts come to little fruition, until finally one day, after a week of focus, you reach stage three. In this stage, you rely on the app to guide your focus. Things are actually getting done and you’re amazed at how such a simple thing has reigned in your potential for productivity. And the one day...

One day, you reach the fourth and penultimate stage. You no longer need the app. Simply having the icon on your phone is enough to deter you from using your precious time doing anything extracurricular... including even using the app. All focus had finally become internalized, and the app, being a mere external vehicle, also seems to waste your potential for focus.

In the final stage, your phone vanishes, app and all. I’ve obviously not reached this stage as I’m reviewing from my phone, but you get the point.

App really does work, if you’re willing to put in the work yourself. Otherwise, it’s useless.

title: Love it!! Please add forest animals
body:
This mom is completely addicted to this app, I’ve been using it since July, and so have my kids. I love the idea of this app and find it so helpful to just tell the kids to Go Grow a Tree if they need a break or need to finish homework. 

Here’s my problem - I’ve unlocked almost everything except for a couple trees I really don’t like.  While I could just keep growing different combinations of trees and bushes, what I really wish I could do is to add forest animals. 

I’d like to be able to earn various forest animals to my existing forests, or maybe start with the animals some times and then add the trees, or add a couple trees and sprinkle animals in. For the shorter time frames smaller animals like birds, butterflies, bunnies, lizards, squirrels, bats, etc. and for the longer time animals like deer, elk, wild pigs, and other regular animals found in the forest. I think the animal options here are endless and also would really make the forests look cool.  The animals would just “grow” exactly like the trees and bushes do.  The animals should match the various kinds of trees that are available. Some regular, some tropical (for palm tree), etc. 

Any chance of animals coming soon?

Also the smaller animals should cost less coins and the bigger ones more coins. I find it annoying that currently the bushes cost the same as the trees. They are smaller and therefore shouldn’t cost the same as the larger trees.

title: Really helpful, would like more customization
body:
This really does keep me from getting distracted by my phone. I want the tree to grow and I am motivated not to hurt it. 

It also works as a timer. You can set it up beside your computer and see the tree grow until it's time for a break. This is a nicely visual method for those of us with terrible time sense, more useful than a numerical countdown.

The tree doesn't die instantly if you leave the app. You can switch away for about 3 seconds, which is important for me because I use my phone for music or audio books all day, and a few seconds is just long enough to switch radio stations or whatever. You can also use the lock screen and the camera safely, talk to Siri, and answer phone calls. So all the really important functionality is still available to me. 

I think the app would be a lot stickier if there were more options for customizing the forest besides unlocking tree types. I would like to arrange my trees and choose background colors and grass colors. I'd also like to be able to zoom in more to see my trees bigger. The Christmas trees were soooo cute and I wish I could keep them!

One interesting thing about the app is you can't just buy trees. You can only buy powerups that increase your rewards for using the app. In a way, that's frustrating, because I am impatient haha! But it genuinely motivates me more to use the app. I admire the creator for refusing to take the easy money and ensuring their app is as effective as possible.

title: Great app and idea, but could you consider adding this feature?
body:
Hello,

First off, I love this idea and the app is well designed and visually appealing, great job on that! If you could add the option to have an unlimited timer, and the ability to pause that timer, this app would be exceptional. I guess not so much a timer, and more of a stopwatch since it would be counting time forward. It would be really cool to have multiple trees grow in a day, maybe one tree every two hours or something. I like keeping track of how much time I spend studying, but I can't pause the app's timer if, for example, I want to grab a quick bite or use the bathroom. Maybe an option to not kill the tree if you exit the app would be nice, too. I understand that the point of the app is to get people to not use their phone and be productive, but some of us have note card apps on our phones (ex. Anki) that we use, and so I would want the time spent doing note cards on my phone to also count towards growing trees! 

So basically I'm asking for a stopwatch feature to the app, that would be amazing!

I love the variety and number of different tree and bush types - it keeps me eager to unlock more - and I love even more so that you can use your points to plant real trees. My only complaints are the limited range of times you can choose and how long it takes to accumulate points for smaller intervals, but these are minuscule gripes. I would highly recommend Forest to everyone looking to gamify putting down their phone to live a better, fuller life!

title: Great App for Focused Production!
body: I find that Forest helps me maintain productivity and lends a solid framework to getting things done. I currently use it while I learn programming, specifically JavaScript. I would tend to either cram to much or get infinitely distracted and not do enough, and through consistent practice I’ve managed to improve my abilities through repeated 30 minute sessions with 5-8 minute breaks in between. I’m not saying the app is a magic cure all - really, it adds a gamified framework that rewards you slightly with points when you complete your timed sessions. However, this importantly makes the act of training your mind into solid shape more focused and fun, and has helped me at least get more productive at work I found very boring at first. I highly recommend this app!

title: Engaging, creative and fun time mgmt tool
body:

As a first year medical student my new lifestyle is mainly studying. I needed a time management and focus tool that would help make studying less painful. 😩 I heard about Forest and was skeptical at first. I did not want to pay for the app since I am cheap and thought I could do it on my own using alternative ways. However I was not successful and decided to buy this app. Since purchasing Forest I have no regrets! 😊 I enjoy the ability to track and visually see my progress. I am a visual learner and am positively reinforced by the forest I am growing and enjoy earning money to unlock more features of the app. What sold me was the social impact of the app where you can plant a tree. Love it! 

Highly recommend and so worth the money spent. Would definitely buy it again.

title: Growing with Forest: Technology and Procrastination
body: In a residential university setting, there are already so many distractions that I face. Most of my friends live just down the hall, social events occur every night, and activities in my dorm and clubs have become a part of my daily life. When I am finally able to escape this frenzy of socialization and sit down in the library, I confront the most tempting distraction of them all: my smartphone. I grew up in a generation of social media and personal technology, and in result, I have become somewhat dependent on the constant stream of information and entertainment available to me on my mobile device. From Twitter to Snapchat to Instagram, there are endless feeds to go through, videos to watch, and people to talk to. In the past, I have taken extreme measures in attempt to squelch my temptations toward the infinite scroll. I have turned off my phone, deleted applications, and logged out of accounts. Despite my efforts, I have always failed to honor my own restrictions, regardless of the fact that it is in my best interests. Because I had not found a solution to my tendency towards distraction, I decided to try ‘Forest,’ a focus-motivating iOS application for smartphones. Forest uses the symbol of a tree in order to motivate users to stop their phone use. When one uses Forest, one sets a timer on the app, and throughout the duration of the set time, a virtual tree grows. If one uses one’s phone as a timer is ongoing, the tree dies. In using Forest as a part of my student workflow, I found that its usability, aesthetic design, and conceptual design work well into my practice of study. Although I observed that the app helps me focus in times of high-intensity study, I will probably not use it in the future for relatively low-urgency schoolwork.

title: Adorably Motivational
body: The cute little trees are just so adorable that I start wanting to put down my phone so I can unlock new ones! I am eagerly awaiting new trees to be added. The user interface is very simple and aesthetic. All in all it’s a great app; the only problem is that sometimes I run into situations where I plant a tree but then end up needing to use my phone for something (like if my mom calls or I have to look up something for homework) and can’t wait for the tree to finish. There is a feature where you can have the app continue counting time after the tree finshes growing, so you can work around the problem by planting a short-time tree and then just continuing to not disturb it. But it would be really great if there was some sort of pause feature, maybe with some limitation like not earning coins if you pause it so that people don’t take advantage of it to ‘cheat’ on their time. Or maybe something where you can erase or reset the time, so you don’t have to feel bad about killing a cute little tree when you actually legitimately needed to use your phone for a minute.

title: This app is awesome
body:
For you study freaks, the Pomodoro Technique is very useful in studying because it emphasizes intense studying. Think of it as intermittent studying where you study intensely, and then take a small break, and then resume again with intense study. 

What is clever with this app is that you can set a pomodoro timer and simultaneously “grow” a tree to create a forest. When that timer is up, take a break; a tree is grown after the timer and you receive coins. You can use these coins to plant real trees. So, this app is designed to increase your productivity and contribute to the environment. I hope this provides whomever is reading this review. 

This app is awesome. Go and download it!

title: Incredibly Useful Time-Management App
body:
I normally don’t write reviews, but this application deserves an exception. At first I thought it might be somewhat useful; I’ve not found that Forest is an integral and important part of my life. The minimal reward sequencing of Forest, planting a virtual “tree” when you’ve completed an adjustable time commitment to stay away from your phone is a friendly and positive reminder to avoid distraction. The fact that the Forest application actually plants trees when you’ve accrued enough focus currency makes this a wholly incredible idea. 

I would recommend it to anyone who finds themselves scrolling away valuable minutes and hours of their lives.

title: Really keeps me off of my phone
body:

There is just something so rewarding about growing a tree while doing something I actually need to do. I have been known to turn it on in serious study mode or when out with friends so I can really be in the moment.

Since the last time I used this, they have added some new capabilities. You can tag trees to say what you were doing while growing your tree. You can use the app with your friends to really make your group focus or actually spend time with each other. And, one of my favorites, you can use the virtual coins you earn from growing trees to plant a tree in real life.

If I have one criticism, it is that they set point values for new trees and real trees entirely too high. It is very hard to raise enough coins to unlock even one new tree type let alone get the funds to plant a tree in real life!

title: Easy, motivating, effective
body:
I downloaded the app for work productivity, but it’s made me hyper-aware of how often I actually pick up my phone. For any task, just having the reminder that my phone is not currently available to me is extremely helpful. I’m realizing that I waste a ton of time that stems from, say, just looking at a text that could wait until later. Moral: don’t think this app isn’t useful because you’re not at a desk all day. It has countless uses. 

I agree with what other users have said about gamification being a good motivator, and the user interface is very appealing. Creating and naming tags produces helpful data. For instance, if you’re concerned about work-life balance, you can see a colorful pie chart with a few simple clicks. 

One thing: I’m fine with how the trees become more “expensive” as time passes. However, it can take a long, long time to gain sufficient coins after awhile. I’m not asking for instant and easy gratification, because that’s contrary to the spirit of the app. I think adding more achievement bonuses (that don’t depend on having friends that use the app or on leaderboard performance) would be great. Unlocking achievements is also rewarding and something to strive for, so I’d love to see more!

title: Excellent for resisting distractions
body: This app really works for me. I’m not sure I really care about growing a forest, to be honest, and there are plenty of distractions out there that do not use my phone, so it would be easy to cheat. But the point of this app is to set a 25 minute timer to stay focused, and then to “nudge” you mentally back on task when your mind starts to wander, or if you think of other things to do—check email, get up and get a glass of water, whatever. This app is a reminder that whatever you think you need to do immediately, it can wait and it’s not that hard to stay focused for the time remaining in your 25 minute work session—and if you succeed you will be rewarded with a new “tree” for your forest (if that is important to you).  It’s also good to see your progress day by day and week by week.

Now I have a much more healthy relationship with my phone! I’m so grateful for that. With the updates over the past few years, this app has been fine-tuned into the perfect product that is worthy of the investment.

However I have just ONE issue. The problem for me is I sometimes over estimate how much time I will need to get my work done. title: My Favorite App!
body:
Forest has made a hugely positive impact on my studies and productivity. The main focus of this app is to stop you from getting distracted, which is already amazing on its own. However, there are also other great things about it. It MOTIVATES me to study because the ability to view how many minutes of work I did in a day/week makes me feel so happy and proud of myself, and it encourages me to plant more and more trees. It also encourages me to continue studying even when the timer is done since you can get more coins. Being able to study with friends is really fun, too! The different trees/bushes you can buy with coins you earn from focusing are all super cute as well. Lastly, I LOVE the idea of being able to plant a REAL tree! (It takes a TON of coins, though, so it takes a while to save up for.) 

Overall, I love this app so much, and every penny was worth it!

title: Nice, Peaceful Little App
body:
I really enjoy using this app, and find it incredibly helpful in keeping my focus on a specific task, like reading or studying or anything that doesn’t require my iPhone.

I pick a tree (my favorite is the Apple Tree), set the timer for how long I’d like to focus, and get to work. It’s very simple, as it should be.

Then I get to work. And many times I’ll forget and absent-mindlessly reach for my iPhone to check Twitter or something, and this app will remind me to stay focused. (Of course, if you NEED to use your iPhone, just use it normally, and the only penalty is that the “tree” you were growing that session will die, and be part of that day’s yard.)

One of my favorite and most important apps on my iPhone. 😀

title: Seems simplistic, but fills a need well

title: This app is charging my life
body:
First, I would like to say thank you to the creators of Forest. I am a highly distractible person, and my life has been a battle for focus (often a losing one). I honestly didn’t think this app was going to work so well. I’ve tried many techniques to attempt to focus, including the Pomodoro technique that this app employs, but have never been successful. Forest is the perfect blend of Pomodoro timer + game.

The reason it works so well for me is that I love trees and flowers. Thus, it provides me a reward that I actually want, that convinces me to not just give up and let the tree die in order to indulge my Pinterest addiction. I have a feeling that if wanting to “grow a forest” isn’t something that interests you, this may not work as well. It does help that you have the opportunity to grow real trees, thus adding an altruistic reason to succeed in focusing.

Forest is also simple to use, has adorable art, and sports a decent selection of trees and bushes to work toward for continued motivation to use the app. I hope they continue to add new types of flora as once I “complete” the game aspect of this app I may not feel as compelled to use it. 

All in all, an elegant solution to phone obsession.

title: This is the only app I’ve ever truly loved
body: I’ve never reviewed an app before, but I love this app so much. I downloaded it after my previous pomodoro timer app, tide, stopped timing correctly, which was literally all it had to do. The timer on this app works, with reliable notifications, and the “gamification” of being focused may seem silly, but it adds a cute and fun element to using a pomodoro timer. Also, the ability to tag how I spend my time (ex: work vs all other things) is an easy way to stay balanced. For instance, I can see if I’m falling behind on daily meditating even if it’s something I’m not conscious of. I can also see someone using this app not necessarily to boost concentration but as a way to literally bar yourself from using your phone for periods of time when you need to be present (ex: during a meeting or with a friend). One more thing I love: I just finished a project that took two months, and I went back and looked at my little forests for that time. Each lil tree helped me get that project done. It’s such a beautiful reminder that everything big happens with many tiny steps!

I also wish there were more even more trees to unlock, that the bushes were less expensive in the store than the trees (because they are smaller and less cool) and that I could whitelist some phone apps that help me be productive. title: Amazing!
body:
Update:

After the developer responded to my review not more than 1 day after I left it, I wanted to update my review. Just as I state below, the app is wonderful. I forgot to mention they also offer a program where you can spend your earned coins to have an organization plant a REAL tree. It’s a really great app. I totally recommend!!

I absolutely love this app. I’ve tried every other anti-procrastination app out there, and none have worked for until I found Forest. The fact that it still plants your dead tree makes you feel guilty because you’ll be able to see it. I feel like that’s the key right there. The saying “out of sight out of mind” really applies here. It’s NOT out of sight so it’s NOT out of mind. I really like this app, it is definitely worth the price

Also, there’s a chrome extension. You manually put in which websites you are NOT allowed to go to, so you can still use your computer for work (blacklist), or you put in the specific websites you ARE allowed to visit, and anything else will kill your tree (whitelist). 

All in all, this is a great app and totally worth the money if you really need help with procrastination.

title: Idea
body: This app is great. What would be really awesome too is if it could have a feature that allows users to track what they spend their time on —it would be a great thing for freelance billing and for getting an overview in general of how much time certain tasks are costing people. For instance, it would be so useful if I could set the timer for say, 25 minutes, and before hitting “Plant,” if I also had an option to name that 25-minute planting session “Storyboard illustration project 01,” or something. And then also to be able to save these task names on a list if such a storyboarding project is going to take me numerous planting sessions, so that I can just select it from a list instead of typing it ever time. With such a feature, I’d be able to look back and see how much time I tracked —good to know for my own productivity, and also to be able to track my work hours all in the same app. Either way, the app is amazing and I’ve already been able to have a real tree planted :)

title: Good App, Could Be Improved
body:
This is a pretty good app for helping people get off their phone during work, class, studying, etc.

Some things that could be improved:
1. If “taking a break” didn’t end the extra minutes you can get. As it is, the feature is useless because you may as well have just quit out of the app anyway.

2. If you could take one break during the original time you had allotted. This would be useful for long work periods and/or if you just needed to make a quick phone call or text.

3. Giving up should give you a dead tree and the alive trees you already earned. If you spend 60 minutes working, then have to end 5 minutes early for something, all your time working shouldn’t go to waste just because of that five minutes!

3b. Dead trees also have “stages” based on how much time you gave up on, where giving up on less time gives you a smaller dead tree.

title: Worth
body:
Does this app improve my productivity and therefore happiness? Yes. Is it perfect? No. Some minor bugs and annoyances. Lacks some features I would like. However, best app like it that I know, and I don’t think a further investment of research/experimentation is likely to be worth it.
 I do recommend it.

Edit: 
Example of minor bug/annoyance: menu animates and collapses into a single position.

Example of “missing” feature: a friend of mine tracks a set of activities that only partly intersects with mine. I would like to be able to either: have shared tags, which is what is tracked in the social competition, or be able to see what her activities are for that day- which incidentally brings up: why can’t I see a friend’s activity for the past week?

There’s a lot more, naturally, but those are the first two gripes that came to mind.

Anyway, solid app regardless.

title: Changed The Way I Spend My Day!
body:
I’m very easily distracted, a habitual phone checker and struggle with my ability to focus. I used to pick my phone up every 2 minutes, even less, just clicking the phone screen to see if anything new had happened or just to check the time (even if I jut checked 45 seconds ago). 

When I downloaded Forest, it took some time for me to actually get the ball rolling and utilising it as much as I can. 

I love knowing how I spend the minutes in my day. I love the productivity I feel when I’m in a flow state and am not distracted by a cellphone going off, I love how much work I get done when I’m not spending one minute refreshing all my apps for every five minutes I’m working on something. 

I use it to time things I hate doing, like the dishes or studying or mopping. I use it for things I love, like yoga, running and reading. 

Plus, every few minutes I spend allows me to receive a coin, which will eventually build up until I’m able to plant a REAL tree. This inspires and drives me to spend mindful minutes in order to have the reward of doing something good. 

All in all, I LOVE Forest. 

I do wish we could customise our dashboard, though. 

10/10

I do not use the app in a competitive fashion, but to help me put down the iPad and get on with my life. I highly recommend this app!

body:
I’m your typical college student/office worker; I’m on my desk at work, home, or school and my phone often keeps me busy doing ANYTHING but my actual work I’m supposed to be focusing on... this app was worth the every penny.

I actually have fun growing as many trees as I can during a work shift, school day, or study sesh in my room. I like that they also have “timed breaks” after you’ve grown a tree. What i do is the Pomodoro Technique: I grow a tree for 25-30mins then take a timed 5min break where I get up and do something else then repeat it!

The visuals of how many trees you’ve done gives this a healthy desire to fill up your little forest each day.

author: Poshposy

title: I LOVE this app! A couple of requests...
body:
This app is the best for those who need a little visual stimulation and extra incentive to stay productive. I truly hate exiting the app during a work session (thus killing my little sapling), and I get a lot of satisfaction from seeing my daily forest grow. The app has kept me from getting distracted by calls, texts, and web-browsing on many occasions. 

A couple of requests: I would love more kinds of ambient sounds to be added to the "store." Also, please create a version for Mac desktop to keep us chronic procrastinators from using distracting apps and websites there! I know that a basic version of Forest exists as a Chrome extension, but it lacks a lot of my favorite features from the app, and doesn't currently block distracting desktop apps. I'm not such a fan of Chrome, anyway (I prefer Safari). In any case, keep up the fantastic work! Oh! And go check out the SleepTown  app by the same developer. It uses the same concept to help people develop better sleep habits, and I can verify that it helps with getting a good night's sleep!

title: The updates and tree variety keep me hooked
body:
I have a newborn son, and we have a routine. He wakes me up about an hour to two hours before I’d normally be up for work. I plant a two-hour tree with Forest and I play with my boy. It was hard at first, because babies don’t appear terribly interesting at times, and I’ve had such a long-time habit of checking the morning news on my phone. But when I plant a tree in the morning, I am so focused on my boy and no longer tempted to read or check my phone. He has my complete attention. 

My wife and I also plant trees right before we sit down to dinner with our kids or watch a movie with them. Forest really helps us to be and stay present with our family. 

I’ve tried other apps that had similar concepts of growing plants and trees, and when they stopped updating I got bored.  Forest has a wonderful variety and updates that have kept me hooked and interested.

title: Secret weapon in war against ADD
body: Forest is a vital tool for me in school. I have been using the app for about 11 months now, and I can say it is completely worth the cost. As a college student who has had to work her way back from a 2.0 GPA to a Masters student, I can say that this app has contributed to my growing success academically. I used to get easily side-tracked by notifications on my phone or even just by scrolling through my camera roll to procrastinate. Now, I like logging hours and knowing exactly how much time per day and week I spend preparing for classes. Knowing I can't take a break until my tree is grown keeps my self control strong. Logging study hours gives me confidence before each lecture or test because I can operationally define how much studying is "a lot of studying." Additionally, I use this app as one of several weapons against symptoms of ADD. I used to justify distractions on my phone, telling myself I couldn't miss out when I got a snap chat or Instagram notification. This app has shown me that those social distractions snowballed into hour-long escapades online and kept me from completing basic academic tasks. I tell everyone who asks about this app that it is fantastic. I love that there are new changes, such as the background sounds and 10 second grace periods. Additionally, the opportunities for awards keep me coming back; since the start of fall term I've made it my goal to plant healthy trees thirty days in a row. My suggestion for this app would be to keep it simple no matter how many updates it goes through. Other apps such as Instagram and Snapchat (though they serve entirely different purposes) are receiving poor reviews because they added too many unnecessary features. As someone who gets distracted easily, I fully appreciate the simplicity of this app and its basic reward system. Please keep the app clean and simple! Thank you for this app!

author: Just A Tree

title: Amazing app!
body:
There are a few things I adore about this app.

The Trees Themselves

The trees are a physical manifestation of all of the time you’ve spent doing things that are important to you. There are many activities where the time spent is more important than the important than the ultimate product of the activity. The trees place a tangible value on that time and that is a wonderful gift. 

The Rewards

This app turns working into a game.
Like any good phone game, you get gold coins and rewards and there are things you can buy with them. For each tree you plant, you earn gold coins that can either be spent on fancy virtual trees or real trees planted through a charity.

You get extra gold coins for hitting various checkpoints (working for a total number of hours, planting trees a certain number of days in a row, etc.)

These are great additional sources of motivation for when you really want to spend the day binging that new Netflix show, but you’re so close to being able to afford that cat-shaped tree, you might as well get an hour of work in.

However, I will say that I REALLY wish there were more checkpoints and achievements available, because working towards those is something I love doing. 

Limited Distractions

A lot of the time when I write, I open apps reflexively. My mind is straining to figure out a plot hole and suddenly I’m scrolling through Twitter, without any conscious intent.

With this app, that reflex is blocked. Every time you reflexively pick up your phone to check twitter/facebook/whatsapp/whatever, you’re reminded that you have **:** minutes left in this session.

Task Tags

The ability to tag how I'm spending my time with various tasks is great. The app lets you view your 'stats’ to see how much time you spend on your respective tasks so you can better visualise how you spend your 'focused’ hours. It's beyond useful if you really want to work on time management. 

Customisable Inspiration

I love adding my favorite inspirational quotes to the home screen.

title: Make it a habit and it's golden.
body:
I've been using this app for years now, forgetting about it here and there. This last year, though, I made it a habit and remember to open it when I have a task that needs my undivided attention. The ease of use is welcomed, in addition to the overall presentation. 

The trees and bush types one can acquire are adorable and thought out, with variations based on the time one sets for the goal. The unlock-able sounds are basically the only ones I don't unlock, but maybe others have uses for it. I also look forward to spending my earned coins on a real tree in the future, now that I use this app often enough to make it a reality. The app does a very good job of explaining the process. 

If I'd ask for any improvement, it would probably be in the layout of the forest. Once a person has a number of trees for the month, the placement feels a little repetitive or uniform. Mirroring a few of the trees might help alleviate this, and possibly grouping related trees/bushes in rounded patterns, instead of rows. 

Otherwise, it is very awesome to see my efforts visualized. Worth the dough in my opinion, if one makes it a habit.

title: Two years strong.
body:

I am aware that there seems to be a Whitelist on the android version of this app, and am curious to know if it would be possible for this version. Ultimately, though, one really ought to stay away from their phone in general when Foresting.

I've managed to convince one of my friends to buy this app, and we spend time reading together and staying focused. Even during the semester, we Forest together for hours on end and are thrilled to know that our distraction-free efforts certainly do pay off.

If you are a firm believer in the Pomodoro technique, you can set a 20/25 minute timer, and then set a break timer when you finish, and then repeat.

Forest has served myself and my friends well. It can serve you, too.

title: Great!
body:
Wonderful app overall, helps me stay focused with work (important for a Masters student approaching finals!), and finally leave my phone alone. The guilt mechanism, to be honest, works wonders for me, especially with being able to plant trees through an NGO after winning a certain number of coins. I've planted two so far and while the going isn't fast -- I only set Forest for specific study tasks (and to help me track how much I've worked) instead of other points in time, it's a great feeling to know that you're doing something that has an actual impact, of a small one. I do worry a little bit about Forest's long run funding for those trees, but we'll have to see, I guess. 

Two criticisms:
 I would personally find if more helpful if you could set a time limit superior to two hours (as opposed to setting reminders to plant a tree, or getting the phone that buzzes once the tree is planted mid-study session). Along that vein, it would be helpful to get extra coins for surpassed time, up to a cap at least. One of the two options would certainly provide great motivation.

My second criticism is that the app only provides a reminder that you're about to kill your tree on select occasions. If your phone is already past the locked screen and on the app, it will give a reminder at the top of the screen. But if you swipe into another app from the lock screen (easily happens if you forgot you had planted a tree), you don't get that reminder/notification. Figuring that kink out, and perhaps increasing the clemency delay to about 10 seconds instead of 3-5 (I'm not sure what it currently is) would be great.

title: An easy way to make a feel-good impact
body:
I'm a medical student (with ADHD) and I've been using Forest for 2-3 months to help me stay focused while studying. It's a win-win: you accomplish more AND help plant real trees. Highlights:
(1) SIMPLE/EASY: you merely dial how many minutes you'd like to stay off your phone, then put it down. The app will alert you when the countdown has finished and you can use your phone again. 
(2) EFFECTIVE: having a tangible goal (i.e. planting a REAL tree) helps motivate you to use the app and to not bail/fail. I used to constantly grab my phone to text someone or Snapchat something funny, but this app prevents me from doing that without feeling like a punishment.
The timer is very flexible (you can turn it on for as little as 5 minutes!) so it's easy to incorporate into your life, e.g. while studying/working, while driving (you  shouldn't be touching your phone anyway), during meetings, during meals, etc. It'll quickly become an easy and rewarding habit. Also, this is a great option for anyone utilizing the Pomodoro method (cycles of 25 mins working/studying, 5 mins off).
(3) ACCOMMODATING: the app will continue running if you receive/answer a phone call (but not texts). Also, when you set the timer it gives you 10 seconds to cancel it; I've set the timer and then immediately remembered I had to return an important call, and I just cancelled the timer without losing points.
(4) REWARDING: I feel elated every time I accrue enough points to plant a REAL TREE. It's a perpetuating feel-good cycle: I feel happy when I use the app, so I want to use it more, so I feel happier, so I use it more, etc etc. 

Overall, I can't say enough about this app! I recommended it to everyone in my med school class, and I absolutely recommend it to you.

title: Get it!
body:
This is one of my favorite apps and I highly recommend getting it. It's worth every penny. 

I felt compelled to write a review because it's succeeded not only on a basic level of strengthening my focus and heightening my productivity — and is beautifully and thoughtfully designed to boot, offering a delightful experience — but I love that the developers didn't program it to goad you into writing a review every other time you open it unlike most apps out there; thank you, developers. 

I definitely have a healthy amount of discipline to not be on my phone all the time, but find that once I go down a rabbit hole, it's sometimes difficult to dig myself out of it. Then, half an hour later, when I surface for airI, I wonder what I've done and if it was at all worth it; usually the answer is "no." 

But with this app in my digital tool belt? Well, give it a whirl yourself— you may just find that you become even more addicted to being off your phone than on it. And you may just find yourself becoming more and more connected to the moment, being more present, and enjoying all that life off of a phone has to offer — a welcome respite in today's world of faster turnarounds, quarterly profit earning reports, and the "faster is better" mentality.

title: Am I missing something?
body:
I really wanted this app to work for me. Unfortunately, it fell short by a lot. 

When a tree is growing, you can't use your phone at all. There isn't a way to designate certain apps as productive. And you can't pause the app, so you have to wait or lose your tree. For this reason, I kept having to change my workflow to do tasks that were legit. That left me resenting the app. 

And I had a really hard time remembering to continuously reset the app (trees only take 25 minutes to grow), leading to frustration when I didn't get credit for the productive time I actually accomplished. I mean, isn't that the whole point? Or is it more about focusing on this company? 

It honestly feels like a pointless app in practice even though I think the idea behind it is great. They need to add settings options that allow users to set their own parameters for success. If you need your phone for work, this app definitely isn't for you. If you want to use it with family members or friends to encourage less phone distraction, it's probably more fun.

title: LOVE but 1 question
body:
I LOVE this app!  I was recently diagnosed with ADHD and a big issue I have is that when I take meds I can focus but sometimes I go a bit over and hyperfocus on the wrong things. This app helps me stop doing that. The most important things one has to do in life is not related to a phone-cooking, cleaning, taking care of kids, work,etc. like many, however, I make my phone the center of my world at times which is esp bad for someone with ADHD.  This has made it possible for me to get a positive reward for doing what I should do anyway. Plus, I love the fact that a real tree  will be planted when I reach 2500 credits. That's a real-world reward I can be proud of!!

I DO HAVE ONE QUESTION, HOWEVER...

Is it possible to add more tags?  I'd rather have the ability to add tags for things I do often so they can be properly tracked over time rather than being able to write in the notes. The "work" tag isn't relevant to me nor does it completely relate to what I do because my work is all over the place. I think many people's jobs are like that these days. I've re tagged as much as I can but it only seems to allow for 5. Can I aad more?  Am I missing it?

Also, I agree with another reviewer who said we sometimes don't get credit for additional time because we get focused and don't realize it's shut off. I'd rather get additional credit if one keeps going.

title: Fantastic app for those who need focus, structure, and productivity
body:
I'm a medical student and for a very, very long time I had trouble focusing for long hours and getting my studying done. My severe lack of productivity was becoming such a strong source of stress for me on top of the demand for school, and feeling discouraged and unmotivated didn't help.

Then I discovered this app a week ago. I've already turned my productivity around. The fun and cool, and no-nonsense way this app makes sure you're productive is incredibly creative and simple. Grow trees, and if you distract yourself, it dies. It's a great concept that builds structure and focus because, let's face it, the dead trees in your forest are such a turn off. The app /makes/ you want to be productive and play by it. 

I love it and I'm such a fan of this app. I would pay 10x the price for it. Its aesthetics are nice, the motivational quotes are great, and it functions well. I get excited for every update for this app now!

Keep up the great work!!

title: A Great Motivational App for Writing, Studying, Everything!
body:
This is a GREAT app to keep you motivated and focused. I'm a writer, blogger, and student. I use Forest to track my writing and see how much time I've put into the app. I love the feature that allows you to see how much (and when) you spend your time; the pie chart that lists all your activities for the day, week, and year; and best of all: the trees.

The trees motivate me most of all because I'm such a visual person. There are different species that you must unlock, making every hour spent on this app worth it when you see your vast, sprawling forest of pine trees, cherry blossoms, and bushes. You can set a timer for as little as 10 minute bushes (I have a lot of these) to a tree of 120 minutes. The trees change appearance according to how much time you put in. The more time you put in, the prettier the trees are. 

This app helped me write a book. I'm a huge procrastinator, but focusing for 2+ hours a day honed my time to writing my book. I can't wait to see what it will do for me in college.

Forest is worth all the time and money I put into it.

body: This app is really cute and the idea of growing your own forest is great. I've downloaded other focus timer apps and this one was the only one that really motivated me to be focused. Despite its creativity, it lacks flexibility. The timer is only limited to max 2 hours. Not that I would want to focus for 10 hours.. But wish I had the flexibility to choose greater number of hours if I wanted. However, I understand why the creators have limited it to two (simplicity of the dial and most people probably won't need to focus for more than 2 hours..) Perhaps the option can be included in the settings to set your own maximum hour? Also note that the timer can only go in increments of 5 min. Additionally, as one reviewer mentioned, it does not kill the tree if I use another app while using the timer. It will only kill if you choose "give up". Otherwise than these, I would give it 5 stars!

title: Nice app but needs more tree options
body:

For example, have a graduated price scale for tree purchases (rather than every option being worth 500 coins). Also, it would be great if some of the trees generated more coins at a very slow rate, as extra incentive to plant/tend the trees. I would pay good money for an even slightly more complex version of this that felt more game-like. 

Finally, it would be great if after a certain threshold you could purchase coins to plant real-life trees. You'd still have incentive to be productive, but more real trees would also get planted. Which is important and a great side-outcome.

title: Sheer Genius
body: This is one of those apps that has become so essential and transformative in my life - both because *it* works so well, and because it inspires *me* to work well - that I'm always worried the people behind it will either get bought out or simply not get enough traction to keep going. Essentially, the genius of it is that it creates an emotional and literal landscape for the time we invest in ourselves. In today's world, when everything we do has become so abstracted, this is the perfect disruption through a child-like, visual metaphor that not only feels good, feels real, but also (apparently?) makes a real difference in doing good for the environment (your virtual trees can add up to a real tree being planted!). Please don't ever stop! This should be the top app.

title: Game Theory and The Silent Game

Everybody would try to stay silent and the one who stayed silent the longest would win. The goal for the parents being that the children stay silent and well behaved while providing the children with a challenge, or a game, to be as silent as possible for as long as possible. This app is kind of like your mom telling you to stay off of your phone for "X" amount of time. X = Time you set. If you  stay off of your phone for the time you set for yourself then you get a beautiful virtual tree and some coins to put towards new species of virtual trees or towards planting a real tree in real life. I love this app and I think it was worth the $3. Kudos to the developers for devolving an app that you literally do nothing but wait.
